pages.label: A NOTE FROM ME
pages.title: Why I wanted this report
pages.deck: An author's note
blocks: I wanted to sit down with one question: what actually changed in India after 2014? It sounds simple until you start reading the numbers. One chart talks about roads. Another talks about jobs. Both may be telling you something real, while leaving out the part you need to understand it.

I write at MisterLove because I like taking a difficult subject apart until it becomes clear. This report follows that approach. I want someone who normally closes a long article after two paragraphs to be able to follow the whole thing. You should not need an economics degree to understand what is happening around you.

The comparisons shared by The Matrix India gave this project a starting point. I have treated those charts as questions to investigate. Wherever possible, the numbers here lead back to the organisation that collected or published them. A figure can be correct and still give the wrong impression when its date, definition or starting point is missing.

I have kept the improvements, the problems and the awkward gaps. If a survey began after 2014, I say so. If a figure is a forecast or a budget plan, I name it as one. If two numbers cannot fairly be compared, I explain why.
There is no final grade for the country here. I want you to finish with a clearer understanding of income, work, prices and public money, and enough information to form your own view.

For readers meeting me here: I'm Lovepreet Singh, a researcher and writer, founder of Lovelace, and an MBA student in Business Strategy and Analysis. My work at MisterLove brings together questions about society, history, public policy and technology. Clear writing is the thread running through it.

pages.label: THE SERIES
pages.title: Six parts. One country.
pages.deck: This volume starts with money and work.
blocks: India is too large a subject for one crowded document. These six parts follow the same approach: show the earlier number, show the recent number, explain what changed, and make the limits visible.
Economy, income, prices, jobs, banking, public money and trade
Roads, railways, airports, power, water, housing and digital access
Health, nutrition, education, poverty and living conditions
Farming, industry, business, science, space and defence
Crime, safety, institutions and the environment
State differences, international rankings and the original charts

The full series is planned at about 168 pages, including notes and sources. This is the completed first volume. The other five are planned volumes, not included in this file. Page targets may change when the material needs more or less room.

Pages 4-8 explain the numbers, GDP, income, prices and wages. Pages 9-14 cover work, women, spending, poverty and inequality. Pages 15-20 examine borrowing, public spending and banking. Pages 21-23 cover trade, external debt and investment. Pages 24-25 revisit the economic chart. Sources are on pages 26-28.
Start at the beginning if the terms are new. If one subject matters more to you, go straight to that page. Every topic explains its own main terms.

pages.label: READ THIS FIRST
pages.title: What does “before and after” mean?
pages.deck: The dates are part of the number.
blocks: For a yearly figure, 2013-14 is usually the nearest full financial year before the change of Union government in May 2014. A financial year runs from 1 April to 31 March. So 2025-26 means April 2025 through March 2026. It is already a completed year at this report's cut-off.

A survey labelled 2023-24 may follow a different calendar. The consumption survey ran from August 2023 to July 2024. The older labour survey used July to June. Its 2025 edition uses January to December. The period is written wherever it matters.
The amount in the money of that year. Prices have not been removed.
Adjusted for changing prices, using a specified base year.
Per person: the total divided by the population.
The gap between two percentages. From 10% to 15% is 5 points, or a 50% relative rise.
A figure that can be revised as better information arrives.
Budget Estimate is a plan. Revised Estimate is an updated plan. Neither is automatically the final amount spent.
One lakh is 100,000. One crore is 10 million. One lakh crore is one trillion rupees. A billion dollars is 100 crore dollars; it is not a billion rupees. The currency matters.

“Latest” here means a release checked by 2 October 2026. It does not mean every measure describes October 2026. Some reliable surveys take years to appear. Blank evidence is left blank; a future target is never counted as an achieved result.

pages.label: 01 / THE SIZE OF THE ECONOMY
pages.title: A bigger economy. How much bigger?
pages.deck: GDP counts production across the country.
blocks: GDP, or gross domestic product, adds up the value of final goods and services produced inside India. A finished shirt counts; adding the full price of its cotton again would count the same production twice. Shops, farms, factories, software and many other activities contribute to the total.
Real GDP growth, same base series

In that historical series, the money value of annual output was about 2.94 times the earlier level. That does not mean India produced 2.94 times as much. Part of the increase reflects higher prices. Nor does it mean each household received 2.94 times as much income.

MoSPI introduced a new GDP series with base year 2022-23 and updated it again in August 2026. In the latest released quarter, April-June 2026, nominal GDP was ₹88.27 lakh crore and real GDP growth was 7.8% over April-June 2025. Both sides of that quarterly calculation use the new series.

The historical table above deliberately retains the older series for its long comparison. Its 2024-25 number is no longer the latest revised GDP level. The 2026 quarterly figure is shown separately because a quarter is not a full year and the statistical method changed. Dividing the two would produce a misleading answer.
Production tells us what the country can generate. The next question is how much of that reaches a person, and how much that person's money can buy.
pages.note: Historical series and current quarter are separate comparisons; no cross-series growth rate is calculated.

pages.label: 02 / PRICES
pages.title: Why lower inflation still feels expensive
pages.deck: A slower price rise is still a price rise.
blocks: Consumer inflation, August 2026, year on year
Food inflation, August 2026, year on year

The first number is a whole-year average. The later two compare one month with the same month a year earlier. They are useful dated readings, but they are not a matched pair of annual averages. August 2026 uses the new CPI base of 2024=100 and is provisional.

Imagine the same basket costs ₹100, then rises to ₹110. Inflation was 10%. If it next rises to ₹115.50, inflation has fallen to 5%. The basket has still become dearer. That is why “inflation is lower” can be true while a family is still struggling with the bill.

CPI means Consumer Price Index. It follows a weighted basket of household purchases. Food, rent, transport and other items do not receive equal weight. A family spending most of its income on food can feel a different squeeze from one spending more on travel or services.

The new basket is meant to reflect newer spending patterns. This also means a long comparison needs the official treatment of the series change. Simply taking an old index number and dividing it by a new one will not tell you the rise in prices since 2014.

The Matrix chart's 2.1% is not the latest monthly CPI reading at this report's cut-off. Whatever period a chart uses, it needs to name that period. For your own budget, compare the prices you pay with the growth in your take-home income. That is where the pressure shows up.

pages.label: 03 / INCOME PER PERSON
pages.title: The average Indian is not an average
pages.deck: A national average is a useful starting point, not a payslip.
blocks: At the prices of each year

These figures come from the same historical national-accounts series in the January 2026 Economic Survey. They are annual amounts per person. The later figure was provisional. This table is a consistent older-series comparison, not a claim to show the latest rebased income estimate.

The nominal figure rose by about 160%. The real figure rose by about 67%. The smaller real increase removes the price changes built into the national accounts. Over eleven years, that real increase works out to roughly 4.8% a year when compounded. These percentages are calculations from the table.

Net national income allows for the wearing out of productive assets and includes residents' income from abroad, net of income going abroad. Dividing it by the population gives per capita income. Children and people without earnings are in that population too.

Now imagine five people earning ₹10,000, ₹10,000, ₹10,000, ₹10,000 and ₹1,00,000 a month. Their average is ₹28,000. Four of the five receive much less. Their median, the middle person's income, is ₹10,000. This is an illustration, not an estimate of Indian incomes.

A rise in average income matters. It tells us the economy generated more income per person on this measure. To understand everyday life, we also need wages, job stability, consumption and the distribution of the gains. None of those can be read straight from the average.

pages.label: 04 / WAGES
pages.title: What did workers actually earn?
pages.deck: Monthly salary, business earnings and daily wages are different measures.
blocks: Regular wage / salaried men, per month
Regular wage / salaried women, per month

These PLFS annual averages use workers' current weekly status. Salary covers the preceding calendar month; self-employment earnings cover the last 30 days. Casual pay is daily and excludes public works. Amounts are nominal. Sampling changed in 2025, so the years are not strictly comparable. This is a recent picture, not a wage series from 2014.

The rows show why a single statement about “wages” can be too broad. The reported male salary average increased; the male casual daily average was almost unchanged. Workers can face very different outcomes inside the same growing economy.

These averages do not follow the same individual over time. A change in who enters a job category can move the average. Nor is a daily wage a monthly income: someone paid ₹455 for ten days receives much less than someone finding work on twenty-six days.

To test buying power, pay must be adjusted for a price index covering the same period. Comparing a 2025 annual wage rise with August 2026 inflation would be a date mismatch. For example, a 6% pay rise with 5% inflation gives a real rise of about 0.95%, calculated as 1.06 divided by 1.05, minus one.
The useful questions are therefore about the pay rate, the number of days worked, prices, and how predictable the next payment is.

pages.label: 05 / EMPLOYMENT
pages.title: What counts as having a job?
pages.deck: The headline unemployment rate leaves out part of the story.
blocks: In the labour force, as a share of adults
Working, as a share of adults
Unemployed, as a share of the labour force

These PLFS annual periods run from July to June. The starting point is 2017-18 because that is when this survey series began. It must not be relabelled “2014”. A longer employment history needs the older surveys and a careful explanation of differences.

The labour force means people working or seeking and available for work. Its share of the population is called LFPR. The worker population ratio, or WPR, counts only the people working. The unemployment rate asks what share of the labour force is without work. Its denominator is smaller than the whole population.

Consider 100 adults. If 60 are in the labour force and three of those are unemployed, the unemployment rate is 5%, not 3%. The other 40 can include students, people doing household work and others outside the labour force. They are not all recorded as unemployed.

A worker may have a monthly salary, run a shop, do casual labour or help without a separate wage in a family enterprise. “Employed” does not promise good pay, full-time hours or a secure contract. The usual-status measure looks mainly across the preceding year; weekly measures capture a shorter window.

The old survey series records both higher participation and lower unemployment over the period shown. That is useful evidence. The next step is to examine the type of work and earnings, rather than treating every counted worker as someone with a comfortable salaried job.

pages.label: 06 / THE RECENT JOB PICTURE
pages.title: Work is widespread. Secure work is another question.
pages.deck: The complete 2025 annual survey is the recent reference here.
blocks: Unemployment, adults aged 15+ in the labour force
Workers with regular wage / salaried work

The first four rows use different populations from the last three. The job-type rows divide employed people into groups and add to 100%. The youth unemployment figure is for young people in the labour force; it does not mean 9.9% of all young people are unemployed.

The survey's sample design changed from January 2025. The ministry explicitly says the results are not strictly comparable with earlier annual PLFS reports. A line drawn through 2017, 2024 and 2025 without marking that break would look more certain than the evidence permits.

Self-employment can mean a successful business, a small farm or work taken up because better options are scarce. Regular salary also does not automatically mean a written contract, paid leave or pension cover. The categories tell us the form of work; they do not measure its whole quality.

For a young person trying to begin a career, the youth figure is often more relevant than the all-age average. For a household trying to pay rent every month, steady earnings and reliable hours can matter more than the simple fact of being counted as employed.

pages.label: 07 / WOMEN AND WORK
pages.title: Participation and independence are different questions
pages.deck: More recorded work needs to be read alongside pay and control over money.
blocks: Within the older survey design, women's participation increased by 18.4 percentage points. That is a substantial rise in the share of women recorded as working or looking for work. The 2025 row belongs to the revised survey and should not be read as a clean 1.7-point fall from 2023-24.

A woman helping on a family farm or in a family shop can count as employed without receiving a separate salary. That work contributes to production, but it does not automatically give her an independent income she controls. Unpaid household care is also economically valuable, although it is treated differently in these employment statistics.

The 2025 survey places 64.2% of employed women in self-employment and 18.2% in regular wage or salaried work. Its reported average monthly salary for women is ₹18,353, compared with ₹24,217 for men. These broad averages are not a comparison of men and women doing exactly the same job for the same hours.

Differences in occupation, hours, seniority and location all matter. So can barriers such as childcare, safety, transport and access to suitable work. The figures alone cannot say how much of the pay gap each factor causes.

The practical question is whether a woman can choose worthwhile work, receive a fair income and decide how to use it. Participation is one part of that picture. Pay, time and freedom of choice complete much more of it.

pages.label: 08 / HOUSEHOLD SPENDING
pages.title: How much does daily life consume?
pages.deck: Spending per person brings the discussion closer to the kitchen table.
blocks: These HCES figures exclude the imputed value of specified free items received through welfare programmes. Imputation means adding an estimated money value for something received without payment. Mixing a series that includes those values with one that excludes them changes the comparison.

At current prices, the rural amount is about 2.88 times its earlier level and the urban amount about 2.66 times. After the published price adjustment, the increases are about 45% and 38%. These are changes over roughly twelve years, not one year.

Monthly per capita consumption expenditure, or MPCE, divides household consumption by household members. A five-person household with MPCE of ₹4,122 has about ₹20,610 of measured monthly household consumption. That multiplication is an illustration. It does not say every rural family spends that amount or has five members.

The surveys changed their questionnaires, coverage of items and interviewing approach between 2011-12 and 2023-24. The table is the published comparison, with those limits. It should not be treated as a perfectly unchanged measuring instrument.

Consumption is not the same as salary. A household can use savings, borrowing, transfers or goods it produces itself. Higher measured consumption is relevant to living standards, but it does not by itself tell us whether the household is financially secure. The next page asks how many people remain below specific spending thresholds.

pages.label: 09 / MONETARY POVERTY
pages.title: Fewer people below the line. Which line?
pages.deck: A poverty rate only makes sense when the threshold is visible.
blocks: The April 2026 India Development Update reports these estimates using consumption surveys. The $3 line is the international extreme-poverty threshold. The $4.20 line is commonly used for lower-middle-income economies. Raising the threshold captures a larger group with limited resources.

PPP means purchasing power parity. It adjusts for differences in what money buys across countries. These are international dollars at 2021 purchasing power. Multiplying $3 by today's dollar-rupee exchange rate would give the wrong local threshold.

On these measures, the reduction is large: 24.5 percentage points at the extreme-poverty line and 41.6 points at the higher line. The World Bank estimates about 35 million people were still below the extreme-poverty line in 2023-24. That is about 3.5 crore people.

Moving just above a line does not make a person comfortably middle class. A family may still be one illness, crop loss or lost job away from difficulty. The threshold is a way to count a defined deprivation; it is not a complete description of a decent life.

These estimates also span 2011-12 to 2023-24, including years before 2014. They cannot assign the whole fall to one administration. Changes in survey methods and the construction of comparable consumption measures affect the estimate. Monetary poverty, multidimensional poverty and hunger measure different things. Part 3 will examine those differences in detail.

pages.label: 10 / WHO RECEIVES THE GAINS
pages.title: Poverty and inequality can move in different directions
pages.deck: Income is money received. Wealth is what is owned, minus what is owed.
blocks: Suppose one person earns ₹10,000 and another ₹1,00,000. Later they earn ₹15,000 and ₹2,00,000. Both have more money. The poorer person's position has improved, yet the income gap has widened. Falling poverty and rising concentration at the top can therefore happen together.

These are research estimates, not a direct government census of every person's income and assets. The researchers combine surveys, tax information, national accounts and information on very wealthy people. The World Inequality Report 2026 also discusses India's high concentration of income and wealth.

The date matters: a report published in 2026 does not automatically turn every underlying observation into 2026 data. The table here deliberately keeps the 2022-23 observation year attached to the values. It does not invent a matched 2014 observation from a different source.

Consumption surveys answer another question: how much households consume. A wealthy household can save a large part of its income. Its spending share can therefore be much smaller than its income or wealth share. A consumption-inequality measure cannot simply replace an income-inequality measure.

The exact concentration estimates depend on how missing or under-recorded income at the top is handled. That deserves scrutiny. It also deserves to be read alongside the evidence of falling poverty, rather than assuming one cancels the other.
For everyday life, the issue is access: who can absorb an emergency, buy a home, fund education or take a business risk? Average income alone leaves those differences almost completely hidden.

pages.label: 11 / GOVERNMENT BORROWING
pages.title: The gap between receipts and spending
pages.deck: The fiscal deficit measures a year's financing gap.
blocks: The fiscal deficit is total government spending minus its receipts other than new borrowing. It is a flow over a year. GDP is the whole economy's annual output, so 4.4% of GDP does not mean 4.4% of the government's budget.

CGA's provisional 2025-26 accounts show ₹49.05 lakh crore of spending and ₹33.86 lakh crore of non-debt receipts. The gap is about ₹15.19 lakh crore. Figures are rounded here from the accounts; the source reports a 4.40% deficit ratio. These are unaudited provisional actuals, not the earlier Budget Estimate.

The 2026-27 figure is a plan for a year still in progress. The historical and current ratios also reflect the GDP estimates used by their publishers. GDP revisions can change a ratio even when the rupee borrowing amount stays the same. Do not read the tiny difference between 4.5 and 4.4 as a perfectly precise measure of performance.
Borrowing can help pay for useful long-lived assets or support activity in a downturn. It also creates future interest costs. The amount, purpose, financing cost and future income all matter.

The two endpoints hide the years in between, including the pandemic. A fair assessment needs that path as well as the endpoints. These figures cover the Centre. State finances must be added with care to assess government as a whole, without double-counting transfers between governments.

pages.label: 12 / DEBT AND INTEREST
pages.title: The old bills travel with the new budget
pages.deck: Debt is the outstanding stock. A deficit adds to the financing need.
blocks: These ratios describe central government debt in the Budget's framework. They are not the combined debt of the Centre and every state, and they are not India's external debt. The GDP assumptions are those of the February 2026 Budget, before the later national-accounts rebasing.

The Matrix chart uses 51.6% for 2013-14 and 56.1% later. I have not established a common debt definition and GDP vintage for that pair. I therefore do not use it to calculate a precise change. Historical liabilities figures can differ because of exchange-rate valuation and which liabilities are included.

Debt is what remains to be repaid at a point in time. The fiscal deficit is a year's gap. A government can reduce its annual deficit and still add to its debt. A debt-to-GDP ratio can fall while the rupee debt rises, if nominal GDP grows faster.

The provisional 2025-26 accounts put central interest payments at ₹12.43 lakh crore. Against revenue receipts of ₹33.02 lakh crore, that is about 37.6%, calculated from CGA's figures. In plain language, a large part of recurring receipts is already committed to interest before other uses are considered.

A government is not identical to a household: it can tax, refinance debt and shape economic activity. It still faces choices. More money committed to interest can leave less room for other priorities unless revenue grows, borrowing rises or spending changes.
The useful question is whether debt can be serviced while maintaining essential services and productive investment. One debt ratio, read alone, cannot answer it.

pages.label: 13 / PUBLIC INVESTMENT
pages.title: More spending on assets. Then comes delivery.
pages.deck: Capital expenditure is a budget category, not a completed-project count.
blocks: The first amount is ₹1,87,675 crore in the Budget's historical account. The second is ₹10,69,119 crore in CGA's provisional accounts. The cash amount is about 5.70 times the earlier level. That is a nominal increase across twelve years, before adjusting for construction and other costs.

Capital spending includes acquiring or creating assets and certain loans or investments. Roads, railway works and equipment are familiar examples. The Centre can also give grants that create assets elsewhere; those grants are not all booked under its own capital-expenditure heading.

For 2025-26, direct capital spending was about 21.8% of total central expenditure, calculated as ₹10.69 lakh crore divided by ₹49.05 lakh crore. The Matrix chart's 22.1% corresponds closely to revised budget amounts. Actual spending and revised plans should keep their labels.

It is tempting to call every capital rupee good and every recurring rupee wasteful. That misses how services work. A new hospital needs doctors, nurses, medicines and maintenance. A school needs teachers. Many useful costs recur each year.

The more demanding test is what the spending delivered: a functioning asset, the people using it, the time or cost saved, and the upkeep it needs. Announced allocations, money spent and completed projects are three different stages. Part 2 will follow that distinction through physical infrastructure.

pages.label: 14 / TAXES AND SUPPORT
pages.title: Where the money comes from, and who it helps
pages.deck: Gross tax, net tax and subsidies answer different questions.
blocks: ₹11.34 lakh crore, provisional at the time

Gross central tax receipts are counted before the states' share is transferred. Net tax revenue is what remains for the Centre after the relevant deductions and transfers. Placing gross receipts in one year beside net receipts in another produces a false comparison.

The 2026-27 gross number is a budget plan, not money already collected. A larger cash total over a long period can reflect a bigger economy, rising prices, tax changes and better collection. It does not by itself measure the tax burden on a typical household.

CGA's 2025-26 major-subsidy total includes about ₹2.28 lakh crore for food, ₹2.11 lakh crore for fertilisers and ₹0.14 lakh crore for petroleum. The displayed components are rounded. This heading is narrower than all welfare spending: pensions, health programmes and many other forms of support appear elsewhere.

A subsidy can reduce a price or support access to a basic need. Its effect depends on who receives it, whether it reaches them and what it costs to deliver. Spending less is not automatically better; spending more is not automatically more effective.

The same care applies to GST. A total GST collection series begins after the 2017 introduction of the system. Writing “zero GST in 2014” would not mean there were zero indirect taxes then. A serious comparison must include the taxes that GST replaced.

pages.label: 15 / BANKS
pages.title: Bad loans became a smaller share of lending
pages.deck: The improvement matters. So does the route taken.
blocks: Gross non-performing loans, scheduled commercial banks

An NPA is a loan classified as non-performing under banking rules, generally because required payments have remained overdue beyond the applicable limit. The gross NPA ratio compares these bad loans with total gross advances. “Gross” is before deducting provisions, the amounts banks set aside for possible losses.

The later ratio is lower by 2.3 percentage points. In simple terms, a smaller share of the recorded loan book was classified as bad at that date. That supports a healthier banking system, but it is not a measure of how many borrowers are debt-free.

The path was not a steady fall from 2014. Recognition of stressed loans changed during the clean-up, including RBI's Asset Quality Review in 2015. Banks can reduce NPAs through repayment, recovery, restructuring that meets the rules, sales and write-offs. A growing total loan book can also lower the ratio.

A write-off changes the bank's accounting. It does not automatically cancel the borrower's obligation or mean that the full amount was recovered. Those outcomes need separate evidence. Likewise, a low bad-loan ratio today does not guarantee that every new loan will be repaid.

RBI's June 2026 report also records strong lending growth and examines banks' ability to handle stress. Its stress scenarios are tests of possible future conditions, not forecasts that a crisis will occur. For a borrower, the further questions are whether credit is accessible, affordable and suited to the income that must repay it.

pages.label: 16 / FINANCIAL ACCESS
pages.title: A bank account became much more common
pages.deck: Access is a real gain. Use and control are the next questions.
blocks: These Global Findex figures count ownership of an account at a financial institution or with a mobile-money provider. They are survey estimates for adults, not the number of accounts. One person can own several accounts, so an administrative account total cannot simply be divided by the population to measure access.

Overall ownership rose by 35.9 percentage points between the two survey years. The large gap between women and men in 2014 had almost disappeared in the 2024 estimates. Small differences such as the later 0.4-point female lead should not be overinterpreted without considering sampling uncertainty.

An account can make it easier to receive wages or transfers, store money and make payments. But an account with no balance, one controlled by somebody else, or one that is difficult to access is a different experience from a regularly used personal account.

To judge financial inclusion more fully, look at activity, independent control, savings, affordable borrowing, service costs and the ability to resolve problems. Having the doorway is valuable; it does not tell us everything about using the room.

The later figures were collected in 2024 and published in the 2025 Findex edition. They are not observations from 2026. The 2014 survey is also a calendar-year observation, not a clean measurement taken just before the May change of government. This is a strong decade-long comparison of access, with those dates kept visible.

pages.label: 17 / SELLING TO THE WORLD
pages.title: Exports grew. Goods and services both matter.
pages.deck: Keep the basket and currency the same.
blocks: The later combined total is about 85% above the earlier one in dollar terms. Spread over twelve years, that works out to roughly 5.3% a year when compounded. These are calculations using the displayed, partly rounded values; they are not inflation-adjusted export-volume growth.

The ministry's later 2025-26 estimate separates roughly $442 billion of goods from $421 billion of services. Goods include physical products. Services can include software, business services and other activities sold to customers abroad. Comparing old goods-only exports with a new goods-plus-services total exaggerates the change.

The original April 2026 combined estimate was about $860.09 billion. Services data were then partly estimated and were updated later. This volume uses the later rounded $863 billion figure and retains its estimate label. Extra decimal places would imply precision that the selected release does not provide.

The latest partial-year release reports combined exports of $399.27 billion during April-August 2026, against $345.55 billion in the same months of 2025. That is a like-period increase of 15.55%. Five months must be compared with five months, not with a whole year's exports.

Export earnings can support firms, jobs and foreign-currency receipts. Gross exports are not the same as domestic value added: producing an exported item may require imported parts, fuel or services. Imports also need to be considered before drawing a conclusion about the country's external balance.
pages.note: US dollars throughout. Nominal values; services estimates may be revised.

pages.label: 18 / THE OUTSIDE BALANCE SHEET
pages.title: More foreign debt can coexist with a lower debt ratio
pages.deck: External debt covers money owed to non-residents by several sectors.
blocks: External debt as a share of GDP

The September 2026 RBI release provides these historical and recent figures in the same table. The dollar debt stock increased by about 74%. Its share of GDP was lower. Those statements can both be true because the economy is larger. The chart's earlier 23.3% is not the March 2014 ratio in this RBI table.

External debt is not just the Union government's borrowing. Companies, banks and other borrowers are included. Nor must every external loan be denominated in dollars: “external” refers to the creditor being a non-resident.

Reserves are foreign-currency assets and other reserve assets held by the monetary authorities. They provide a buffer, but they are not an unlimited fund for meeting every private debt. The reserve-to-debt ratio is also different from import cover, which asks how many months of imports reserves could pay for at a specified import rate.

A current account deficit is a flow, not this debt stock. It combines trade in goods and services with income and transfers across borders. The 2013-14 deficit was reported as 1.7% of GDP. This volume does not certify the chart's later 0.6% without a matched balance-of-payments release and revision date.

The timing of repayment matters as much as the total. Debt falling due soon, currency changes and the ability to refinance can create pressure. A single external-debt ratio cannot capture all of that risk.

pages.label: 19 / FOREIGN INVESTMENT
pages.title: Money entering the country is only one side
pages.deck: Gross FDI is different from net FDI.
blocks: 2024-25, updated series in the fact sheet

These are total FDI inflows, not just equity inflows. DPIIT's March 2026 fact sheet includes equity, estimated reinvested earnings and other capital. The latest annual total is about 2.62 times the 2013-14 level, an increase of roughly 162% in nominal dollar terms.

FDI, or foreign direct investment, generally involves a lasting ownership interest in an enterprise. It can bring money, technology, management links and access to markets. Its effects depend on the investment's form and what the business actually does.

Gross inflow counts the inward side. Net measures also deduct specified outward flows, such as investor exits or repatriation; broader net direct-investment balances also account for residents' investment abroad. Always check the definition in the source. A strong gross total can coexist with a weak net figure.

Buying an existing business and building a new factory are both capable of attracting FDI. They do not create the same amount of new productive capacity at the moment of the transaction. Reinvested profits can count even when fresh money does not cross the border that month.

The fact sheet marks components as estimates and the recent data as provisional. The total is useful evidence of the scale of inward investment. It is not a direct count of factories built, jobs created or money permanently staying in India. Those outcomes need their own evidence.

pages.label: 20 / READING THE MATRIX CHART
pages.title: Where the economic comparison needs care
pages.deck: First eight rows of the fifteen-indicator chart.
blocks: The chart is a starting list of claims. The notes below explain what this volume established, changed or left unresolved. A “before” and “after” pair needs the same concept, period and source treatment.
The old 4.7% used the 2004-05 factor-cost framework. The 2011-12 GDP series reports 6.4% for 2013-14. New 2026 data use another base. Do not treat the pair as unchanged measurement.
The old figure is an annual average. The latest monthly CPI reading checked is 4.82% for August 2026. A whole-year / one-month mix needs explicit labels.
Broadly matches the reported endpoint ratios here. Keep Centre-only scope, GDP vintage and provisional status visible.
22.1% matches revised budget amounts closely; the provisional actual share is about 21.8%. The older 11.7% denominator was not independently established here.

pages.label: 21 / WHAT THE CHART CANNOT SETTLE
pages.title: The remaining rows, and the question of credit
pages.deck: A change after 2014 does not, by itself, identify its cause.
blocks: RBI's current historical table gives 23.9% for March 2014 and 20.8% for June 2026. State the dates and revision vintage.
Reserve date and import denominator: past imports or projected imports? Not independently certified here.
Bank coverage, observation dates and adjustment for mergers. One annual rate is not the growth rate for an entire era.
Specify which subsidies, actuals or estimates, and GDP vintage. “Major subsidies” is narrower than all welfare spending.
Name the IMF or other release and whether the later value is observed or forecast. It is not an Indian government output.
A PPP-weighted contribution needs a published calculation and year. It is not India's share of world income.
Growth rank among major economies: 3 to 1
Define “major”, the countries, period and forecast status. Ranking is separate from income per person.

Several chart rows remain unresolved here; they are not promoted into verified facts. Part 6 is planned to extend the chart and ranking audit. The two posts originally supplied, covering infrastructure and Scheduled Tribe crime, belong to Parts 2 and 5 respectively.

For responsibility, timing is a starting clue. A result can reflect Union policy, state policy, earlier investment, private effort, technology and world conditions. Establishing how much one policy caused requires evidence beyond two endpoints. Recognising that does not erase an achievement or a failure; it makes the explanation more accurate.

pages.label: A NOTE FROM ME
pages.title: A country is also the things that work.
pages.deck: An author's note
blocks: Part 1 began with money, work and prices. This part starts closer to the front door. Is there a road you can use in the rain? Does the tap run? Can you reach a hospital, make a payment or get home without losing half your day? These are ordinary questions. Together, they tell us a lot about a country.

I wanted this volume to explain infrastructure without making it sound like an engineering textbook. A gigawatt should mean something to the person paying an electricity bill. A kilometre of metro should mean something to the person trying to get to work.

The chart shared by The Matrix India made a striking claim about how much was added after 2014. Some of its comparisons hold up well. Others need a different starting date, a clearer definition or a newer figure. I have kept the original claims visible so you can see where the report agrees and where it changes the comparison.

I also want to keep two things in view at the same time: building something and making it useful. A house on a sanction list is still a promise. A house completed is a physical result. A house that a family can safely live in is the reason for doing the work.

At MisterLove, I write about society, history, public policy and technology in plain language. I'm Lovepreet Singh, founder of Lovelace and an MBA student in Business Strategy and Analysis, working toward doctoral research. This report follows the same habit: take the claim apart, explain it, and leave the evidence where the reader can find it.
I am not asking you to memorise these numbers. I want you to understand them well enough that the next dramatic chart takes a little less effort to read.

pages.label: YOUR WAY THROUGH THIS VOLUME
pages.title: From the highway to the kitchen tap
pages.deck: Part 2 of the six-part India report card.
blocks: How to read the figures and the chart percentages
National highways, faster roads and rural roads
Electric trains, passenger and freight use, dedicated freight corridors
Metro, airports, ports and inland waterways
Power capacity, renewable energy, electricity supply and cooking gas
Internet access, digital payments and who can use them
Checks on every row of the Matrix infrastructure chart

The figures are organised by what the service does. Transport moves people and goods. Power and gas supply energy. Water, sanitation and housing support daily life. Digital networks help people communicate, pay and use services.

Most earlier observations are from March 2014 or 2013-14. Some programmes and surveys began later. Those dates remain visible. The recent column means the latest suitable figure checked for that comparison, not a measurement of everything on the same day.

Part 1 is complete. This is Part 2. The remaining planned volumes cover health and education; farming and industry; crime, institutions and environment; and state differences and international rankings. Their figures are not silently folded into this volume.
The research cut-off is 2 October 2026. A 2026 publication may describe 2025 activity. A target for 2028 is still a target. Each table tells you which kind of date you are reading.

pages.label: HOW TO READ THE COMPARISON
pages.title: A bigger number needs a clear meaning.
pages.deck: The unit, the date and the stage of delivery come first.
blocks: A stock is what exists at a date, such as railway length or tap connections. A flow is activity during a period, such as annual cargo or monthly payments. A change in stock is not automatically entirely new construction. A financial year such as 2013-14 runs from April 2013 to March 2014.

One lakh is 1,00,000. One crore is 1,00,00,000, or ten million. MMT means million metric tonnes. MTPA means million tonnes per year of handling capacity. A port able to handle 100 MTPA has capacity; it may actually handle much less cargo that year.

A gigawatt, written GW, is 1,000 megawatts of power capacity. It describes how much power equipment can produce under the relevant conditions. A kilowatt-hour, or one electricity unit on a bill, measures energy used over time. Capacity and annual electricity generation are different.

The Matrix chart's percentage uses the later total as its denominator. If a network goes from 100 km to 200 km, the extra 100 km is 50% of the new total. The usual growth rate is 100%, because the increase is divided by the earlier 100 km. Both calculations are valid; they answer different questions.

That chart formula works best for a consistently measured stock. Annual coal production or defence exports are flows. Their increases are not the share of a physical network built. Recognised startups are an administrative category, and tap-water coverage is a household percentage.

Sanctioned means approved. Under construction means work is progressing. Commissioned means put into service under the relevant reporting rules. Usage tells us what people or goods actually did. We keep those stages separate because each is a different part of the story.

Finally, a change after 2014 does not tell us exactly who caused it. Union and state decisions, local bodies, private investment, earlier plans and technology can all contribute. These comparisons establish recorded changes; they are not a calculation of political credit.

pages.label: 01 / NATIONAL HIGHWAYS
pages.title: The main road network became much longer.
pages.deck: National highway length is one part of India's roads.
blocks: A national highway is a road in a designated national network. It is not every road in India. State highways, district roads, village roads and city streets are counted under other headings. The larger later number therefore describes one important network, rather than every route a person can travel.

Imagine a map with 91 km of a particular road category. A rise of about 61% would take that category to roughly 147 km. That gives a feel for the scale. The actual national figure is a thousand times larger.

The network can grow through new alignments, extensions and the declaration of existing roads as national highways. Widening an existing stretch can improve its capacity without adding the same number of route kilometres. So the difference of 55,285 km should not be described as 55,285 km of brand-new road built on previously roadless land.

Road kilometres and lane kilometres also differ. A 10 km four-lane road is 10 road km but 40 lane km. Adding lanes can make construction substantial while the route length remains 10 km. Mixing the two units makes an increase look larger or smaller than it is.

What does this mean in daily life? A useful new or improved connection can shorten a journey and help goods reach a market. The actual gain depends on where it goes, congestion, tolls, maintenance and access from the surrounding area. A bigger national total cannot tell you whether your particular journey became easier.
pages.note: The later endpoint is the dated ministry report. Network growth includes changes in designation.

pages.label: 02 / FASTER AND WIDER ROADS
pages.title: More lanes and expressways. Different counts.
pages.deck: The road category must stay the same in both columns.
blocks: Four-lane and above NH, June 2026 backgrounder
Operational national access-controlled corridors, Dec 2025 review

Four-lane and above tells you the road's width in traffic lanes. Access-controlled tells you how traffic enters and leaves it: vehicles normally use planned interchanges rather than every roadside turning. A wide highway and an expressway are therefore not automatically the same thing.

The chart's expressway pair, 1,000 to 6,700 km, was not independently reproduced for a consistent all-India definition in this volume. National corridors are a narrower series than a total that might also include state expressways. The official national figure above cannot simply replace an all-India total without explaining the change in scope.

Construction speed also varies by year. The ministry's annual table reports 12.1 km a day in 2014-15, 36.5 in 2020-21, 33.83 in 2023-24 and 29.21 in 2024-25. The last of those is 10,660 km across the year. The peak rate was not maintained every year.

These annual construction figures can include improvement works, not just entirely new roads. The 2014-15 observation is also after the change of government. It should not be labelled the entire pace of the earlier government.

A faster road can save time when its complete usable stretch connects the places people need. An awarded project, an opened section and a complete corridor are separate milestones. Safe crossings, emergency response, local access and upkeep remain part of the result.
pages.note: Road series and later dates differ by row. No single expressway total is certified here.

pages.label: 03 / RURAL ROADS
pages.title: A village road can change an ordinary day.
pages.deck: PMGSY counts programme work, including construction and upgrades.
blocks: Cumulative constructed across phases, July 2026 release

PMGSY is the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana. It began in 2000 to provide all-weather rural road connectivity. Later phases also improve important routes and links to facilities. It existed before 2014 and continued afterward.

The June backgrounder separately reports about 4.11 lakh km completed during 2014-2026. That is work during the later period, not a later cumulative total of only 4.11 lakh km. The July cumulative figure of nearly 7.97 lakh km makes that distinction clearer.

Programme work is not the same as the length of a unique national rural-road network. An upgraded road can be counted as work even though a route already existed. Different programme phases also have different purposes. Adding all their work lengths does not prove that every kilometre was a first-time connection.

Think about a farm connected to a market by a track that becomes unusable during heavy rain. A durable road can make the trip more predictable. It can also help a school bus or ambulance reach the settlement. The benefit comes from the usable connection, not from the sign announcing the project.

Eligibility matters. A habitation is a settlement, and programme rules use population thresholds and special provisions for some difficult areas. “All eligible habitations connected” would not mean every small settlement in the country has every kind of road. Maintenance and bridge condition determine whether the connection stays useful.

pages.label: 04 / ELECTRIC TRAINS
pages.title: Most broad-gauge routes now have electric wires.
pages.deck: Electrifying a route is different from building a new one.
blocks: An electric locomotive receives power through equipment above the track. Electrification provides that system on a route. The railway can then run suitable electric trains there. A route may be decades old even when its electric equipment was installed recently.

Route km measures the distance between places along the network. Track km also counts parallel tracks. A 100 km route with two running tracks is still 100 route km, although it has 200 running-track km. Electrification statistics must not be silently compared with total track length.

The displayed electrified length is about 3.2 times the ministry's earlier baseline. The increase is about 48,072 route km. That is a major change in the type of traction the network can support. It is not a claim that the whole railway became 3.2 times longer.

There is a historical reporting difference worth keeping visible. The older revised railway statistical summary records 21,614 electrified route km for 2013-14. The 2026 backgrounder uses 21,801 for its retrospective 2014 comparison. The table above retains the later ministry vintage; it does not pretend both historical totals are identical.

Electric trains can reduce direct diesel use and support efficient operation. The wider environmental effect depends on how their electricity is generated. Wires alone do not settle punctuality, ticket availability, crowding, track quality or safety.

Broad gauge describes a particular distance between rails. The 99.6% figure applies to that network. It should not be expanded into a claim that every railway, every route or every train in India has become electric.

pages.label: 05 / WHAT THE RAILWAY CARRIED
pages.title: More freight. Fewer passenger journeys.
pages.deck: Physical use belongs beside the infrastructure total.
blocks: The earlier figures come from the revised railway statistical summary. The recent figures come from the ministry's annual release. On these reported measures, freight is about 59% higher, while passenger journeys are about 12% lower. The recent headline data are not a substitute for the final detailed statistical accounts.

A passenger journey is a trip, not a unique person. Someone making repeated trips can be counted repeatedly. Railway passenger counts also combine different kinds of travel, including frequent suburban journeys and longer-distance trips.

A lower total does not prove that every type of railway travel declined. Nor does it, by itself, establish why the total changed. To understand the cause, we would need comparable suburban and non-suburban data, passenger kilometres, service availability, fares and changes in reporting.

The historical series shows the pandemic's disruption plainly: 808.6 crore journeys in 2019-20, 125 crore in 2020-21 and 351.9 crore in 2021-22. A later recovery from that low point can be real while the level remains below an older year. Both facts belong in the same explanation.

Freight tonnes count how much was carried. Tonne kilometres also count how far it travelled. Carrying one tonne for 1,000 km is a different amount of transport work from carrying it for 100 km. Higher freight loading therefore needs distance and commodity mix for a fuller interpretation.

For a traveller, the practical questions remain simple: can I get a seat, can I afford it, and will the journey be safe and reasonably dependable? A larger capital budget or more electric routes cannot answer those questions on its own.
pages.note: Earlier freight: revenue-earning tonnes. Later figure: ministry headline loading; final detailed accounts may refine comparability.

pages.label: 06 / DEDICATED FREIGHT CORRIDORS
pages.title: Routes for goods trains.
pages.deck: A real addition, with a history that began before 2014.
blocks: Eastern and Western dedicated freight corridors
Commissioned before 2014 in the stated project account

Freight means goods. A dedicated freight corridor is a railway designed mainly for goods trains. Separating much of that traffic can reduce competition for space on conventional lines that also carry passenger trains.

The August 2026 parliamentary answer says both corridors were commissioned. The September announcement describes the last links being joined. These are dated accounts of completion. Their 2,843 km is the stated combined length, not all Indian freight routes.
The zero means no commissioned kilometres of these corridors in the cited before-2014 account. India already had freight trains and goods routes, and preparation for this project had begun.

The project company, DFCCIL, was registered on 30 October 2006. Planning, finance, land acquisition and construction have different timelines. Earlier preparation and later commissioning both belong in the history.

Imagine trucks and commuter buses competing on one road. A separate route for many trucks can help both services if its junctions and connections work. Dedicated freight capacity follows a similar idea.

The practical tests are dependable delivery, useful factory and port connections, costs and actual use. The chart's 100% is calculated from zero commissioned kilometres. It does not measure the share of planning, spending or preparation that occurred after 2014.

pages.label: 07 / METRO AND CITY TRAVEL
pages.title: Metro reached more cities.
pages.deck: A network can expand without serving every neighbourhood.
blocks: Metro is urban rail designed for frequent travel within a city and its connected areas. The reported route length is about 4.7 times the 2014 level, an increase of 907 km. The Matrix chart's rounded 1,000 km recent endpoint is below the later official snapshot used here.

Cities covered tells us how widely the system has spread. It does not tell us how much of each city has a useful connection. A small operating section and a large connected network can each put a city into that count.

Ridership normally counts trips or entries under the operator's method, not unique people. A commuter travelling to work and back can generate two trips. The national daily total also needs its reporting date and operator coverage; it is not a household survey of how many Indians can afford metro travel.

Consider a 15-minute train journey that requires a 30-minute trip to the first station and another 20 minutes from the last station to work. The whole commute is 65 minutes, before waiting. This is an example, not a measured national average. It explains why feeder buses, walking routes and interchange design matter.

A metro can offer dependable travel where demand and connections support it. Its usefulness also depends on fares, operating frequency, accessible stations, safety and maintenance. A completed line that few people can conveniently reach has a different value from a well-used one.

Keep regional rapid transit, ordinary metro and water-based urban transport labelled separately where the source does. They can all improve mobility, but a kilometre of one is not automatically interchangeable with a kilometre of another.
pages.note: The recent daily ridership is a reported 2026 snapshot, not a matched full-year average.

pages.label: 08 / AIRPORTS AND REGIONAL FLIGHTS
pages.title: More places can connect by air.
pages.deck: An operating airport is not a promise of frequent cheap flights.
blocks: UDAN routes operationalised, cumulative to 15 July 2026
Airports, heliports and water aerodromes connected by UDAN

The operational-airport total is higher by 91, or about 123%. That does not mean 91 entirely new airports were all built from scratch. A total can change through new facilities, revived facilities and changes in operating status or coverage.

UDAN is a regional air-connectivity programme launched in 2016. It supports selected routes to improve access to underserved or unserved places. Its route count is a different measure from the total airport count.

The UDAN snapshot also reports over 1.68 crore passengers cumulatively. Cumulative means across the programme's operation up to that date. It is not 1.68 crore passengers in a single year. A person taking several flights can be represented several times.

Heliports and water aerodromes serve different aircraft and operations from conventional airports. The 95 connected sites should therefore keep all three categories in the label. Adding them to the national airport total would risk counting overlapping facilities twice.

A route that was operationalised at some point is not automatically a route running every day now. Airlines, schedules and services can change. Before judging regional access, look at current flights, continuity, the fare people actually pay and the time needed to reach the airport.

A useful local flight can save a long road trip to a distant airport. For someone unable to afford a ticket, the airport alone does not create affordable access. Infrastructure and the travel experience need to be assessed together.
pages.note: The chart shows 164 airports. The selected later official snapshot reports 165; the date is kept visible.

pages.label: 09 / PORTS
pages.title: Ports can handle more. They also handled more.
pages.deck: Capacity and actual cargo are separate rows.
blocks: All Indian ports in the matched ministry table

A port is where ships load and unload. Capacity is the amount it can handle annually under the source's method; MTPA means million tonnes per year. Throughput is the cargo actually handled. One is a capability, the other an activity.

On the matched figures, capacity roughly doubled: about 101% growth. Actual cargo increased by about 72%. Both are substantial increases. They are different because the ability to handle cargo is not the same as the quantity arriving to be handled.

The Matrix chart uses 800 to 2,760 MTPA. Its starting point is not the all-ports 2013-14 capacity in the matched ministry table. Comparing an older major-ports figure with a later all-ports figure would change the basket. This volume uses all ports in both columns instead.

A port can be physically capable of handling more cargo while ships still wait for a berth, paperwork or a road and rail connection. Faster unloading can also be undermined by slow movement outside the port. The full delivery chain matters.

A ship-turnaround figure is a measure of time, but averages can cover different vessel types and operations. One must keep the scope and period consistent before comparing them. Capacity alone is easier to measure than the complete experience of moving goods from a factory to a customer.

More cargo is not automatically more domestic value added. Ports also handle imports, raw materials and different kinds of bulk freight. The cargo mix is needed before making a claim about the value of what India produces.

pages.label: 10 / INLAND WATERWAYS
pages.title: More freight moves on rivers and canals.
pages.deck: A declared waterway and an operating one are different.
blocks: Annual inland cargo, matched ministry table

Inland waterways are navigable routes within the country, including rivers and canals. National Waterway status identifies a route under the legal and development framework. It does not make that route commercially usable all year.

An operating route needs a usable channel, vessels, terminals and land connections. Water depth, river conditions and maintenance affect what it can carry. A legal declaration is an earlier stage than dependable transport.

The Matrix chart compares five earlier waterways with 32 later ones. Five is the earlier declared count; the matched table gives three operational waterways in 2013-14. Compare declared with declared, or operational with operational.

The chart's earlier cargo figure of 29 million tonnes differs from the roughly 18 million tonnes in the matched table. The dated pair used here shows about twelve times the earlier cargo, with the rounded baseline visible.

Water transport can suit heavy goods when the route and terminal connections fit the shipment. Distance from the river, loading time, deadlines and seasonal reliability matter. It is not automatically the best option for every product.

Cargo tonnes do not measure the full environmental effect or the share of physical waterways built. Ferries, tourist cruises and freight are different uses. Adding their counts would not give one meaningful transport total.
pages.note: The matched 2013-14 cargo baseline is rounded to 18 million tonnes in the parliamentary table.

pages.label: 11 / POWER CAPACITY
pages.title: India can generate much more power.
pages.deck: Installed capacity is the equipment total, not the electricity bill.
blocks: Increase in the displayed recorded stock

The later total is about 2.23 times the earlier level, or roughly 123% higher. That is a comparison of installed generation capacity. It is not a claim that electricity generation or every household's supply grew by exactly the same percentage.

Think of capacity as the kitchens available, and generation as the meals actually produced. Some kitchens operate often; others operate only at particular times. Equipment and output must be counted separately.

The CEA's August 2026 table gives 250.21 GW of fossil-fuel capacity and 304.334 GW of non-fossil capacity. Non-fossil includes renewable sources and nuclear power. It is broader than renewable energy alone.

By capacity, the table reports 54.88% non-fossil and 45.12% fossil. Coal alone is 40.47% of the total. Those are equipment shares. They do not say that 54.88% of all electricity generated during the year came from non-fossil sources.

A solar plant cannot generate its rated power continuously through the night. Other plants also have outages, fuel limits or maintenance needs. Supply has to match demand at the moment it is needed, using generation, storage, transmission and operating arrangements together.

Installed equipment can grow while a locality still has interruptions because of distribution faults. Better operations can also improve supply without as much new generation equipment. The chart shows a rounded 540 GW; this volume uses the dated August CEA total.

pages.label: 12 / RENEWABLE ENERGY
pages.title: Solar grew especially fast.
pages.deck: Keep large hydro in or out consistently.
blocks: The solar total is about 59.5 times the earlier value. A tiny starting point makes a large multiple possible, but the absolute addition also matters: about 165.2 GW. Wind is about 2.8 times its earlier level. Not every renewable technology grew at the same pace.

Renewable sources include solar, wind, hydro and forms of bioenergy under the official categories. Large hydro means larger hydroelectric projects; whether it is included changes the total substantially. In August 2026, the CEA figure excluding large hydro is about 243.49 GW, compared with 295.55 GW including it.

The older 76.38 GW is the retrospective inclusive baseline in the June 2026 government backgrounder. Solar and wind use MNRE's historical series. These source vintages remain labelled, rather than being silently replaced with older differently classified totals.

The chart's renewable pair, 54 to 248 GW, was not reproduced on a clearly consistent basis here. It needs dates and an inclusion rule for large hydro. It should not be read as a universal total of all clean-energy equipment. Nuclear power is non-fossil, but it is outside the renewable total used above.

Large additions to solar capacity create more ability to generate electricity when conditions allow. Turning that into dependable supply throughout the day also requires grid connections, flexibility and storage or complementary sources. A target or a tender award is not installed capacity.

Rooftop solar can reduce purchased electricity. The outcome depends on sunlight, system size, costs, maintenance and billing rules. A national capacity total does not mean every roof has panels or every home has a zero bill.
pages.note: GW figures converted from MW. Current renewable totals include the categories shown in CEA/MNRE reporting.

pages.label: 13 / ELECTRICITY THAT REACHES PEOPLE
pages.title: Longer hours of electricity.
pages.deck: Connections, supply and reliability are different measures.
blocks: The March 2026 reply gives these later averages. Rural supply rose by 10.1 hours. It calls the earlier year FY2015, or 2014-15; the backgrounder calls it 2014 and supplies the urban baseline. These figures do not promise uninterrupted supply to each household.
Averages hide differences between states, seasons and localities. A business affected by brief interruptions needs more than a total-hours measure. Voltage quality and repair time also matter.

Transmission moves large amounts of electricity over longer distances. Distribution carries it through local substations, transformers and lines to consumers. A strong national grid can still meet a weak local link.

Circuit km is a counting unit for transmission circuits, not simply the distance along a map. For example, two circuits running over the same 100 km route make 200 circuit km. The table covers lines at 220 kilovolts and above; it does not include every local wire.

Transmission crossed five lakh circuit km in January 2026. The release gives 71.6% growth since April 2014. The chart's roughly 42% divides the increase by the later total instead. The different denominators answer different questions.

A household connection gives access to the network. Regular supply, an affordable bill, safe wiring and prompt repairs make it useful. The February 2026 backgrounder repeats an older urban average of 23.4 hours; the March reply gives 23.6 for FY2025. The dated versions are not identical.
pages.note: Supply hours: FY2025 in the March 2026 reply, not a new household survey. Transmission milestone: 14 January 2026.

pages.label: 14 / GAS FOR THE KITCHEN
pages.title: Gas reached more households.
pages.deck: PNG is piped natural gas; LPG usually arrives in cylinders.
blocks: Long-distance pipelines carry gas to consuming areas. City-gas networks distribute it to homes and businesses. A pipeline passing an area does not mean every home there has a kitchen connection.

The recent pipeline total is about 79% above the historical ministry figure. It comes from PNGRB's March 2026 publication, but that particular table explicitly dates the pipeline data to December 2025. The publication month must not replace the observation date.

A domestic PNG connection provides a fixed pipe to a household. It is different from a commercial or industrial connection. The earlier approximate reach of 25-26 lakh homes is a figure stated in the March 2026 Prime Minister's speech, rather than an independently reconstructed household survey.

PNGRB records 1,69,49,377 domestic connections for March 2026, of which 1,07,25,930 were billed connections: about 63%. The regulator distinguishes having a connection from being billed for use. The exact administrative meaning matters; the gap cannot automatically be called permanent abandonment.

The August 2026 ministry release also describes converting unbilled connections into working connections. Its later 1.74 crore total is a connection-stock figure. This report does not invent a later billed-use percentage from that stock.

Piped gas can remove cylinder deliveries where service is dependable. LPG provides another route to cleaner cooking where PNG is unavailable. For either fuel, costs, safety and supply matter. A connection alone does not prove that a household can afford enough fuel or has stopped using other fuels.
pages.note: Pipeline observation: December 2025.

pages.label: 15 / WATER AT HOME
pages.title: A tap is a start. Water is the service.
pages.deck: The correct programme baseline is August 2019, not 2014.
blocks: August 2019, at the start of Jal Jeevan Mission

Reported coverage rose by 65.52 percentage points. About 82 of every 100 rural households were recorded with taps in the update, leaving about 18 outside coverage. States and Union Territories report these figures; they are not a fresh survey of water from every tap.

The earlier 16.72% is from 2019. Putting it under 'before 2014' moves it back five years and changes the story. This report keeps the correct programme date, rather than implying the entire recorded addition began in 2014.

The separate 2024 functionality assessment examined selected villages and households. Among households with taps in that sample, 87% had received water during the previous week, 80% received at least 55 litres per person per day, and 76% met the combined functionality conditions. Those conditions concern quantity, quality and regularity.

Fifty-five litres covers daily household needs, not just drinking. For four people, that corresponds to 220 litres a day. A pipe supplying too little or unsafe water provides a different service from a dependable tap.

The assessment's 98.1% connection figure applies to its surveyed villages. It is not India's national coverage. Nor can we multiply the 2026 national connection percentage by the 2024 sample's functionality percentage and call the result a measured national rate for 2026.
Wider access is a substantial reported change. Its everyday value depends on whether water arrives when needed, meets quality standards and can be supplied reliably through changing seasons.
pages.note: Connection coverage and the independent functionality sample answer different questions and refer to different years.

pages.label: 16 / SANITATION
pages.title: Building toilets changed access.
pages.deck: Using them and safely handling waste complete the job.
blocks: Population using improved sanitation: NFHS, all India
12.14 crore by June 2026; programme launched in 2014

The programme count shows a large construction effort. One household toilet can serve several people, so twelve crore toilets is not twelve crore people. The cumulative count is also not a survey of every facility's present use.

The 100% refers to reported rural coverage and 2019 open-defecation-free declarations under programme rules. Open defecation means going outside without a toilet. A declaration does not establish that every Indian has used a safe, maintained toilet ever since.

NFHS measures people in households using improved sanitation, across rural and urban India. Improved facilities separate waste from human contact under its definition; shared facilities are treated separately. This survey percentage cannot replace rural programme coverage. It rose by 21.7 percentage points from 2015-16 to 2019-21. The periods show changed living conditions, not a measurement for 2014 or October 2026.

A usable toilet needs water where the design requires it, privacy, maintenance and safe arrangements for waste. Emptying a pit or tank unsafely can move the health risk to workers or nearby land and water. Access, use and safe disposal are connected, but each needs its own evidence.

Sanitation programmes existed before Swachh Bharat. Zero under a new scheme only means that scheme had not begun. The comparison concerns expanded delivery and use, not the invention of toilets in 2014.
pages.note: Programme coverage is rural. NFHS figures shown here are all India; they are not a like-for-like rural coverage series.

pages.label: 17 / HOMES
pages.title: More homes completed.
pages.deck: Approvals and completed homes are different counts.
blocks: Over 1.25 crore sanctioned; over 1 crore completed/delivered

IAY means Indira Awaas Yojana, the earlier rural housing programme. PMAY-Gramin restructured support from 2016. The row compares annual programme completions, not all homes built; rules and reporting also differ. Annual completions are about 2.45 times the earlier count. A finished home may have been approved earlier. The 26.57 lakh count does not mean every house was approved, started and finished within twelve months.

The August reply lists 4.18 crore houses in allocated targets, 3.91 crore sanctioned and 3.12 crore completed. Targets assign work; sanctions approve it; completions record a later stage. The roughly 79 lakh gap between sanction and completion is not additional completed housing.

The urban milestone combines PMAY-U, launched in 2015, and PMAY-U 2.0, introduced in 2024. The release describes over one crore homes completed or delivered. This wording does not establish an independently surveyed count of homes occupied today.

These totals cover programmes, not the whole housing stock. Rural and urban schemes count homes under different arrangements. Private construction and older housing programmes also existed. Zero under a newly launched scheme is not zero homes in India.

A completed home becomes useful when it is safe and connected to essentials. Location, water, electricity, sanitation, transport and maintenance shape that experience. Construction counts explain one stage; they cannot settle every question about living conditions.
pages.note: Cumulative totals cover multiple years.

pages.label: 18 / INTERNET
pages.title: Internet use grew fast.
pages.deck: Subscriptions count connections; they do not count unique people.
blocks: Broadband subscriptions, excluding M2M in the recent total
110.12 crore, August 2026; not the matched consumer comparison
Average wireless data per subscriber per month

Broadband meets an official minimum speed definition. That threshold changed from 512 kilobits per second to 2 megabits per second over the period. Subscriptions expanded greatly, but the measurement did not stay completely unchanged.

A subscription is a connection or account under telecom reporting rules. One person may have two mobile connections and a home line. Several people may share one device. Therefore 101 crore broadband subscriptions does not mean 101 crore different Indians each have their own dependable internet.

M2M means machine-to-machine: connections for devices such as meters or trackers. TRAI includes about 9.09 crore in its broader August total. The main comparison excludes them from the recent total; the broader total is labelled separately.

Data use measures the amount transferred, not speed or quality. On the decimal convention, 1 GB is 1,000 MB. Moving from tens of MB to tens of GB marks very different use. The average does not describe every subscriber.
TRAI reports average operator revenue of about Rs 7.51 per GB in the March 2026 quarter. This is not the price of every customer's plan. Retail plans bundle amounts, validity and other services.
Living in a covered district does not remove weak signals, phone costs or difficulty using a service. The next page looks at household access and payments alongside the network totals.
pages.note: August broadband data were released on 28 September 2026. The data-use observation is for the March 2026 quarter.

pages.label: 19 / USING DIGITAL SERVICES
pages.title: Using the digital network.
pages.deck: Transactions, households and people are separate measures.
blocks: Households with at least one smartphone
Households with internet access within the premises
Value transferred through UPI in August 2026
The survey asks whether access exists in the home. It does not say every member owns or controls a phone, or can complete digital tasks alone. Its percentages describe 2025, not October 2026.

Among people aged 15-29, the survey reports internet use during the previous three months by 92.7% in rural areas and 95.7% in urban areas. Those figures concern young people in the sample. They do not describe all ages or establish that everyone can use every online public service.

UPI, the Unified Payments Interface, allows payments between accounts through participating services. It began in 2016. A 2014 UPI total is therefore 'not yet launched', not evidence that electronic payments or banking transfers did not exist before 2014.

NPCI's August 2026 table records 24,508.96 million transactions. Ten million make one crore, so that is 2,450.896 crore transactions. Its value figure, Rs 29,82,355.95 crore, is about Rs 29.82 lakh crore. Count tells us how many payment transactions occurred; value tells us how much money those transactions moved.

The same money can move more than once. A payment from one person to a shop and a later payment from that shop to a supplier are both transfers. Adding the payment values does not measure newly created wealth, government spending or GDP.

A useful digital service needs a workable device, connectivity and a way to understand and complete the task. Someone who needs help should also be able to get it. More transactions show widespread use of the system; they do not prove that access is equally easy for every person.
pages.note: UPI is a monthly flow, not a count of unique users. August 2026 was the latest monthly table verified for this volume.

pages.label: A NOTE FROM THE AUTHOR
pages.title: What progress feels like.
pages.deck: A longer life. An easier school day. A bill a family can pay.
blocks: A country can look successful in a chart and still feel difficult to live in. I wanted this part to ask about the things that reach inside a home: whether a baby survives, whether a mother gets care, whether a child can read, and whether there is enough money for ordinary needs.

I write on MisterLove because I like taking a complicated idea apart until it becomes clear. My interests in research, business and technology keep bringing me back to one question: what does a number actually tell us about a person's life? A bigger hospital count and a healthier population are related, but they are different things.

The Matrix India posts started this series. They made me want to put the earlier figure, the later figure and the original source on the same page. In this part I return to its AIIMS, medical-college and MBBS-seat rows, and then widen the picture to health, learning, poverty and living conditions.

I am using 2014 as a point of comparison, not pretending that the country's history began there. Many changes started earlier. The Union government, states, public workers, private institutions and families all helped shape the results. A before-and-after table alone cannot divide the credit between them.

I have kept the dates visible, including the awkward ones. If the latest report published in 2026 measures 2023-24, I say 2023-24. If a new blood-testing method interrupts an older series, I explain the break. I would rather give you an honest gap than a neat number that means something else.
You do not need to know the jargon. Read the figure, then the paragraph beneath it. That is where I explain what it counts, what changed and how to picture it in everyday life.

pages.label: YOUR READING MAP
pages.title: Where to begin.
pages.deck: Each topic stands on its own. The dates travel with the figures.
blocks: How to read the dates, units and comparisons
Life expectancy, infant deaths, maternal care, fertility and vaccination
