Numbered sources; click a title to open the original publication

FY means financial year: April to March. FY2025-26 therefore ends in March 2026. A crop year commonly runs from July to June. A survey can cover a still earlier period. Each table says which one it uses.

One lakh is 100,000. One crore is 10 million. A million tonnes is 10 lakh tonnes; a billion is 100 crore. A tonne is 1,000 kilograms. A quintal is 100 kilograms. These are different ways of writing amounts, not different kinds of progress.

Current-price rupees are the money values reported for that year. They include price changes. More rupees spent or earned does not automatically mean the same increase in physical output or purchasing power. A percentage-point change measures the gap between two percentages: 40% to 50% is 10 points.

The cut-off is 3 October 2026. This volume covers the main national measures in these subjects; it cannot list every crop, industry, invention or military programme. Parts 1-3 cover the economy, infrastructure and living standards. Parts 5-6 will cover institutions, safety, the environment, state differences and rankings.
pages.note: FY2014-15 runs from April 2014 to March 2015 and crosses the change of government. It is not a fully earlier baseline.

pages.label: 01 / CROP PRODUCTION
pages.title: The harvest is much larger.
pages.deck: This measures food produced. Farmer income needs a separate question.
blocks: Foodgrains include cereals, such as rice and wheat, and pulses, such as gram and tur. Rice and wheat are already inside the first row. Adding all three rows would count them twice. The earlier 245.80 million-tonne cereal total sometimes seen in tables leaves out pulses; it is not the full foodgrain total.

The later figures are the third advance estimates, released on 27 May 2026. They are estimates for the 2025-26 crop year, not final audited totals. The 2024-25 final foodgrain figure was 357.732 million tonnes. The newer estimate is about 5.3% above that.

Against 2013-14, the estimated foodgrain harvest is roughly 42% larger. Picture an earlier harvest of 100 tonnes becoming about 142 tonnes. Rice rose by about 44%; wheat by about 26%. These are changes in physical quantity, so inflation does not explain them.

A larger national harvest can come from more land planted, more crops taken from the same land, better yields and different weather. The total alone cannot split the increase between those causes. It also does not show whether every farmer earned more.

For a family growing wheat, the useful next questions are its yield per acre, selling price and cost of seed, labour, water and transport. The country can produce more food while some farms struggle. Availability, food prices and a farmer's profit each need their own evidence.
pages.note: 2013-14 is a final historical figure. 2025-26 is an advance estimate; later revisions can change it.

pages.label: 02 / WATER FOR FARMING
pages.title: More crop area gets irrigation.
pages.deck: Count a field once, or count each crop season. The result is different.
blocks: Net irrigated area counts the land that received irrigation, counting each piece once in the year. One hectare is about 2.47 acres. The increase from 68.419 to 82.416 million hectares is about 20%.

Gross irrigated area counts each irrigated crop season. If the same hectare grows two irrigated crops in a year, it contributes two hectares to the gross count. Gross area rose by about 36%. It can grow faster than net area when land is used for more crop seasons.

The third row says that about 60 out of every 100 hectares counted across crop seasons received irrigation in 2023-24. The earlier figure was about 48. The change is 12.1 percentage points. It is not the share of India's total land, or the percentage of farmers with their own pump.

Water access can reduce dependence on the timing of rain. But being recorded as irrigated does not establish that water arrived in the right quantity, at the right time or at an affordable cost. A field with an unreliable supply can still be in this count.

The report is dated October 2025 and its newest national observation is provisional 2023-24. I have kept that date visible. This is not a measurement of irrigation in 2026. Groundwater levels, water quality and the cost of pumping also matter; environmental pressures are taken up in Part 5.
pages.note: Source units are thousand hectares; the table converts them to million hectares. Gross area counts repeated crop seasons.

pages.label: 03 / FARM-HOUSEHOLD INCOME
pages.title: Two surveys tell the story.
pages.deck: Different dates and definitions. No interchangeable numbers.
blocks: SAS means Situation Assessment Survey. Its first figure describes July 2012 to June 2013; the second describes July 2018 to June 2019. An August 2026 reply still identifies the 2019 round as the latest SAS. It is not the only national survey offering information on agricultural households.

Between the two SAS reference years, average income increased by Rs 3,792 a month, or about 59%. It did not double over that measured interval. This is a nominal rise, in each year's rupees. Higher prices reduce how much of the increase buys extra goods.

The figure covers the household's members and can include crops, animals, wages and other work. It is not one person's salary or crop profit alone. SAS 2019 required a self-employed agricultural member and annual produce worth more than Rs 4,000. Families doing only farm wage labour were excluded. The income comparison deducts paid business expenses.

NABARD, the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development, runs the All India Rural Financial Inclusion Survey, or NAFIS. It reports Rs 13,661 a month for agricultural households in 2021-22. This is a newer reading, but it uses a different survey and eligibility threshold: produce worth more than Rs 6,500, with a self-employed agricultural member. It cannot simply replace the SAS endpoint.

Neither later figure describes income in 2026. Averages also hide differences between families, and counting unpaid family work as a cost changes the result. To judge a claim that income doubled, we need matched definitions, dates and a clear choice between ordinary rupees and purchasing power after inflation.
pages.note: The table labels two separate surveys. A publication year is not its income reference year; no older reading is presented as 2026 income.

pages.label: 04 / MILK, FISH AND EGGS
pages.title: Farming includes much more.
pages.deck: Animals and fisheries are a large part of the production story.
blocks: Milk production was about 80% higher than in 2013-14. Fish production more than doubled, rising about 106%. Egg production nearly doubled, rising about 99%. The fish figure is provisional. These are physical quantities, not the rupee value of sales.

For eggs, one billion means 100 crore eggs. The latest total is therefore about 14,911 crore eggs in a year. It counts production, not the number of people eating eggs or the amount each family can afford.

The dairy report also gives milk availability per person: 319 grams a day in 2014-15 and 485 grams in 2024-25. That earlier year crosses the government change. Availability is production divided across the population; it does not mean every person drank that amount each day.

India was already the world's largest milk producer in 1998. A continued first-place rank and a rise in the amount produced are two separate facts. The later output is much larger, but the leading position did not begin after 2014.

These activities can give a household more than one source of earnings. Their costs still matter: feed, animal care, disease, electricity, storage and transport can affect what the producer keeps. A bigger national milk or fish total cannot establish a bigger profit for every dairy farmer or fisher.

More production also does not guarantee better nutrition in every home. Prices, distribution, diets and who gets the food shape that result. Part 3 examines nutrition directly rather than treating output as a substitute for a health survey.
pages.note: Milk and egg series use the dairy report; fish is converted from lakh tonnes. All production figures keep FY2024-25 as their latest year.

pages.label: 05 / FARM SUPPORT
pages.title: A price promise and a cash transfer.
pages.deck: The announced price, the actual sale and family income are separate amounts.
blocks: MSP means Minimum Support Price. It is an announced support price for specified crops. A quintal is 100 kilograms. Common-paddy MSP rose about 86%, maize about 84% and tur about 97% in ordinary rupees. Different crops received different increases.

An announced MSP does not establish that every farmer sold every crop to the government at that price. Actual procurement, local buyers, crop quality and access to a purchase centre affect what happens at the sale. The table records the policy price, not each farmer's received price.

The 2026-27 paddy announcement uses a cost of Rs 1,627 per quintal and a margin of about 50%. That cost includes paid expenses and an estimated value for family labour, often called A2+FL. It is not the wider C2 cost, which also includes items such as the rental value of owned land. A 50% margin on one cost measure does not automatically mean a 50% profit on every farmer's full costs.

PM-KISAN, introduced in 2019, pays eligible landholding farmer families Rs 6,000 a year in three Rs 2,000 instalments. The 23rd instalment, released on 20 June 2026, transferred Rs 18,880 crore to 9.44 crore farmers. These are that instalment's reported recipients, not a count of everyone working in agriculture.

For a recipient family, the annual benefit averages Rs 500 a month. It can help pay some expenses, but it is not the family's whole income. Adding it to an older survey average would invent a new national income figure; the survey year, eligibility and other earnings would need to be measured together.
pages.note: The MSP comparison uses the same crop and kharif marketing-season series. All price increases shown are nominal.

pages.label: 06 / REGISTERED FACTORIES
pages.title: More people work in factories.
pages.deck: The newest factory survey was released on 30 September 2026.
blocks: Gross value added, Rs lakh crore
Total output value, Rs lakh crore

The Annual Survey of Industries, or ASI, covers the registered factory sector. It does not count every workshop, home business or informal manufacturer. The latest results describe April 2024 to March 2025, although the release came in September 2026.

The first row includes factories in the survey's frame. The second counts those operating. The difference matters: a recorded factory is not automatically a working one. Operating factories rose by roughly 18% over this comparison.

Persons engaged includes workers and other people working in these establishments, such as management and support staff. The total rose by about 74.59 lakh, or 55%. It is a difference between two annual survey estimates, not a count of unique people who got a new permanent job during 2026.

Output is the total value produced. Gross value added, or GVA, subtracts the value of bought-in inputs. Imagine a factory producing goods worth Rs 100 using purchased materials and services worth Rs 60: the value it adds is Rs 40. That amount still has to cover wages and other claims; it is not the owner's profit.

GVA was about 2.53 times the earlier rupee value. Output was about 2.52 times. Both use current prices, so these multiples include inflation and are not physical-production growth rates. Survey coverage also evolves over time; these results describe the ASI sector, not all Indian manufacturing.
pages.note: Source money tables use Rs lakh; these values are converted to Rs lakh crore and rounded. Employment is not a count of workers alone.

pages.label: 07 / STEEL
pages.title: Capacity is not the steel made.
pages.deck: A plant can be able to produce more than it actually produces.
blocks: Capacity means how much plants are equipped to make in a year. Production means how much they actually made. Think of a bakery able to bake 1,000 loaves a day but baking 750. Its capacity is 1,000; its output is 750. Neither number can replace the other.

Crude steel is the steel at an early production stage, before it becomes many finished products. Actual crude steel output more than doubled between 2013-14 and 2025-26, increasing by about 106%. The newer figure comes from the ministry's April 2026 release and is provisional.

The June 2026 compendium puts capacity at over 220.4 million tonnes a year. Capacity also more than doubled against the 2013-14 baseline. The capacity recorded near a year's end and the output made throughout that year do not give a precise utilisation rate simply by division.

The Matrix chart shows 109 to 222 million tonnes. The historical ministry table identifies 109.85 as capacity in 2014-15, a year spanning the government change. It gives 102.26 for 2013-14. Neither is that year's actual crude steel output.

The chart's later 222 is close to the recent capacity scale, but it is not the exact June compendium figure. Without a matching source date, I cannot reproduce that number precisely. What the dated sources do show is a large rise in both productive capacity and actual output.

More steel can support buildings, machinery and transport. It does not by itself tell us the profit of steel companies, the quality of every product, the jobs created or the environmental cost. Those outcomes require separate measurements.
pages.note: The chart row is explained as a capacity claim. The report keeps capacity and physical production in separate rows.

pages.label: 08 / COAL
pages.title: Much more coal. A recent dip.
pages.deck: A long-term rise can contain a year when production falls.
blocks: The latest full-year figure is about 84% above 2013-14. A production level of 100 in the earlier year would be about 184 now. These figures measure coal mined in India; they are not mining capacity or the monetary value of coal.

The newest year is slightly below the preceding one: 1,040.08 versus 1,047.52 million tonnes. That is a fall of 7.44 million tonnes, or about 0.7%. A report card should show both the long-term increase and the most recent change. 'It kept rising every year' would go further than these figures allow.

The Matrix row shows 565 to 1,000 million tonnes. Its earlier number is a rounded version of the historical scale. The later rounded number captures the move past one billion tonnes, but the current full-year observation is 1,040.08. The years need to travel with the numbers.

Higher domestic production can help supply power stations and industry. It does not automatically end imports. Coal comes in different grades, and steelmaking needs coking coal. A country can produce more of some grades while still buying others abroad.

These coal totals should not be mixed with lignite, a different fuel that has its own statistics. Nor should mined tonnes be added to power-generation capacity measured in megawatts. One counts fuel produced; the other counts the power equipment installed.

Supply security and environmental effects are different questions. More coal can support energy availability while increasing pressures that need to be managed. Air quality, emissions and the wider energy balance belong in the environment discussion in Part 5.
pages.note: The table uses full financial years. FY2025-26 ended in March 2026; it is not a partial calendar-year total.

pages.label: 09 / ELECTRONICS AND MOBILES
pages.title: India makes and exports more.
pages.deck: Production value does not reveal how much of each product is made locally.
blocks: The matched table comes from a July 2026 parliamentary reply. Its earlier year is 2014-15, not a strictly pre-2014 baseline. All values are in the rupees of the reporting year. Production counts value made in India; exports count value sold abroad.

All-electronics production became about 6.9 times the earlier value. Electronics exports became about 11.2 times. Mobile production and exports grew much faster. Using the rounded endpoints above gives about 35 times and 173 times respectively; these are approximate ratios, not exact unrounded results.
The release also calls the mobile increases about 33-fold and 165-fold. Those labels do not reproduce exactly from its displayed rounded baselines. The table therefore keeps the endpoints visible.

A phone assembled in India can still contain imported chips, displays and other parts. The value of the finished phone is larger than the value added inside India. This table establishes growth in production and exports; it cannot establish that every component is domestic.

Mobile figures are part of the wider electronics figures. Adding them together would double-count mobiles. Exports are also part of production and sales, rather than an extra amount of GDP to add on top.

To judge how deeply manufacturing has developed, we would also want local component production, design work, domestic value added, worker pay and productivity. A larger sales-value table is useful evidence, but it does not answer all those questions by itself.
pages.note: Rs 1,00,000 crore = Rs 1 lakh crore. Electronics production of Rs 13,11,000 crore is Rs 13.11 lakh crore.

pages.label: 10 / SMALL BUSINESSES AND SUPPORT
pages.title: More registrations need context.
pages.deck: A survey estimate and an online register count different things.
blocks: MSME means micro, small and medium enterprise. The older figure estimates unincorporated, non-agricultural enterprises covered by the National Sample Survey, or NSS. Its scope excludes some registered companies, registered factories and construction. It is not a count of every Indian business.

The newer figure is an administrative registration headline. Udyam and the complementary Udyam Assist system bring firms into formal recognition, including existing informal micro businesses. Registering an old shop does not mean the shop was newly created. Eligibility and coverage also differ from the older survey.

The survey estimated 11.10 crore people employed in its covered enterprises in 2015-16. The August 2026 backgrounder says registered MSMEs employ more than 40 crore. These are different systems, so subtracting them would not give jobs created. The newer headline is not an independent survey of unique, currently active jobs.

A separate industrial support programme is PLI: Production Linked Incentive. It supports additional eligible production or sales across 14 sectors. The September 2026 government summary reports, up to June 2026, Rs 2.6 lakh crore of investment, Rs 23.8 lakh crore of production and sales, over Rs 15.5 lakh crore of exports and 14.6 lakh jobs.

Those PLI amounts are programme totals accumulated over time, not one year's national manufacturing output. Investment is not the government's incentive bill; sales are not profit. Exports overlap with sales, so the amounts should not be added. The reported jobs also do not establish the net jobs caused by the programme compared with what would have happened without it.
pages.note: 2015-16 is after 2014. No percentage-growth claim is made from the unmatched MSME survey and registration counts.

pages.label: 11 / STARTUPS
pages.title: Recognition began in 2016.
pages.deck: India had young businesses before it had this particular official register.
blocks: DPIIT is the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade. Startup India began in January 2016. Recognition is an official status for entities meeting eligibility conditions; it is not a census of every new business, or a guarantee that a recognised firm will succeed.

The rise from 452 in the scheme's first year to about 2.54 lakh is a large expansion of recognition. Part of the early-to-later difference reflects the register building up after it began. New recognition can include a business that already existed before it applied.

The Matrix chart compares 500 before 2014 with 2,30,000 later. The later number is within the scale of the expanding official register, although the September 2026 update is higher. But the earlier 500 cannot be a 2014 count under a recognition system launched in 2016.

I have not found a matching source definition that makes those two chart endpoints the same measure. That leaves the exact 500-to-2,30,000 comparison unresolved. It does not mean India had no startups before 2014, and it does not erase the growth documented after recognition began.

A recognised-startup count tells us about participation in the system. It does not tell us how many firms remain active, earn a profit, survive several years or create secure jobs. Those need business-survival and employment data. Eligibility rules also shape who can enter the count.

A 'unicorn' is a private company valued at at least one billion US dollars. That valuation is an estimate used in investment deals; it is not cash earned, annual production or the founder's money in a bank account. Large startup counts and valuations should therefore be read alongside actual business results.
pages.note: There is no invented zero for startups in 2014. The comparable administrative series begins after the comparison boundary.

pages.label: 12 / RESEARCH SPENDING
pages.title: More money goes into research.
pages.deck: The newest observed total and the projected total are not interchangeable.
blocks: R&D means research and development: work to understand something new or develop a new product, process or technology. GERD means the total spent on this work inside the country across the sectors covered by the statistics. It is wider than the budget of one science ministry.

The latest observed expenditure in DST's 2025-26 statistical publication is for 2023-24. It is about 3.08 times the 2013-14 amount in current rupees. This includes price changes; it does not establish that research activity or its results tripled.

The GDP share asks how large research spending is relative to the economy. At 0.84%, it is roughly 84 paise for every Rs 100 of GDP. The older share uses the 2011-12 GDP base and the newer one the 2022-23 base. That change prevents a perfectly matched comparison.

The 2025-26 figure is projected from recent sector growth rates. It is not a fresh observation of all spending in that year. The report labels it as a projection, so the 0.90% headline should keep that label too.

For research papers, the report uses a US National Science Foundation data series: 78,135 in 2012 and 2,07,390 in 2022. The later observation remains 2022. The count rose about 2.65 times; it measures papers counted in that series, not the quality or usefulness of every paper.

Spending, papers, skilled researchers and useful discoveries are connected, but they answer different questions. A stronger report card needs both resources and results. A larger budget cannot tell us by itself whether a treatment worked, a new machine reached customers or a paper changed what scientists know.
pages.note: DST = Department of Science and Technology. The last row is projected. GDP-base changes and current-price rupees are stated explicitly.

pages.label: 13 / PATENTS
pages.title: More applications. Uneven grants.
pages.deck: Asking for protection and receiving it are different events.
blocks: A patent application asks for legal protection for an invention. A grant means the office accepted an application after examination. One is a request; the other is a later decision. The baseline is 2014-15, not fully before the government change.

Applications were about 2.58 times the earlier count. Indian applicants' share rose by 33.56 percentage points. The all-applicant total also includes foreign applicants seeking protection in India; it should not be presented as a count of inventions made only by Indians.

Grants show a less smooth path. DST reports 1,03,057 grants in 2023-24, followed by 33,504 in 2024-25. The latest level is well above 2014-15 but much lower than that recent peak. Presenting the peak as the newest annual result would conceal the drop.

Applications and grants need not come from the same batch. A patent granted this year may have been applied for years earlier. Dividing this year's grants by this year's applications would therefore not give an applicant's chance of approval.

Changes in grants can reflect the flow and timing of examination as well as the earlier stock of applications. These totals alone cannot identify the cause of the latest fall. They do not prove that inventions suddenly became less useful, or that a particular administrative change caused it.

A granted patent is also not a product already sold. Some inventions reach the market; others do not. Applications, grants, licensing income and successful products are separate steps. For a small inventor, receiving a grant can matter greatly, but the national count cannot tell us the commercial outcome of every invention.
pages.note: DST Tables 30 and 33. Latest verified annual patent counts here describe FY2024-25, not inventions or decisions made throughout 2026.

pages.label: 14 / SPACE MISSIONS
pages.title: Old capability. New milestones.
pages.deck: The story crosses 2014, and it includes setbacks as well as achievements.
blocks: 5 November 2013: launched; 24 September 2014: entered Mars orbit
12 January 2026: anomaly near the end of the third stage

India already had a lunar mission before 2014. Chandrayaan-1 was an orbiter: a spacecraft studying the Moon from space. Chandrayaan-3 demonstrated a soft landing, reaching the surface under control. Orbiting and landing are different technical achievements.

The Mars mission makes the date boundary especially clear. It launched in November 2013 and reached Mars in September 2014. Its planning, construction, launch and arrival cannot all be assigned to one side of the 2014 line.

SpaDeX demonstrated docking: bringing two spacecraft together and joining them in orbit. That is a useful capability for more complex missions. A successful demonstration does not mean every future mission using it has already succeeded.

The 2026 PSLV-C62 mission also belongs in the record. ISRO reports an anomaly near the end of the third stage. A launch taking place is not automatically a successful delivery of its intended spacecraft. Counting only celebrated achievements would leave out part of the programme's performance.

These are selected mission milestones, not a total of all launches. Launch count, satellites carried, mission complexity, reliability and useful data are different measures. One rocket can carry many satellites, so more satellites does not necessarily mean the same increase in rocket launches.
pages.note: Dates refer to actual events, not announcement dates. The Mars mission spans the comparison boundary.

pages.label: 15 / SPACE BUDGET AND NEXT STEPS
pages.title: About twice the full allocation.
pages.deck: Use the same budget stage, then keep future missions separate.
blocks: Budget Estimate is the amount planned at the start. Revised Estimate is the updated plan later in the year. Actual expenditure is what was spent. Comparing the full original allocations, 2026-27 is about 2.02 times 2013-14 in current rupees, not a doubling of purchasing power.

The original 2013-14 budget contains Rs 5,615 crore under the old Plan category and Rs 1,177 crore under Non-Plan. Together they make Rs 6,792 crore. Comparing only the earlier Plan portion with the later full total would inflate the rise.

The 2026-27 budget document also shows that the 2025-26 estimate was revised down from Rs 13,416.20 to Rs 12,448.60 crore. Neither estimate is a final bill. The actual-expenditure row shown here is the 2024-25 net figure in that document.

An August 2026 reply targets the first uncrewed Gaganyaan experimental mission for October-December 2026. Further uncrewed flights and the first crewed mission are targeted by 2027. 'Uncrewed' means without people aboard. These are target dates; they do not count as completed human flights.

The same reply targets a fully operational Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035. It records an approved Rs 20,193 crore programme budget for eight missions. Approval is not the same as money already spent, and a budget spread across missions is not a single year's departmental allocation.
pages.note: Historical allocation categories have changed. The comparison uses full Budget Estimates; all Gaganyaan and station targets retain their source date.

pages.label: 16 / DEFENCE PRODUCTION
pages.title: Defence production value grew.
pages.deck: Production value, spending and readiness are separate measures.
blocks: Defence production reached about Rs 1.78 lakh crore in 2025-26: about 4.07 times 2013-14 and roughly 16% above the rounded 2024-25 value. These rupee totals include changes in prices, the amount produced and the mix of equipment.

The latest production split is about 76% from defence public-sector companies and other public units, and 24% from the private sector. Public production therefore remains the larger part of the reported total. A growing private sector does not mean public units have disappeared.

Production value counts the sector's output. It is not the government's defence budget, the value of exports alone or the number of weapons available to troops. A high-value aircraft, a ship and many small components can all contribute money values without being comparable units of equipment.

The Union's 2026-27 defence allocation is about Rs 7.85 lakh crore. Its capital allocation is about Rs 2.19 lakh crore, including about Rs 1.39 lakh crore earmarked for capital procurement from domestic industry. Capital spending covers longer-lived assets; the wider budget also pays for other needs.

An earmark is a planned allocation. It does not mean every purchase is complete or every rupee has been paid to a supplier. These budget amounts cannot be added to production value as though they were separate pieces of national output.

Domestic production can build skills and supply capacity. Imported components, maintenance, delivery delays and performance require separate evidence. This table records production value; it cannot establish complete military self-sufficiency or combat readiness.
pages.note: The later production values are ministry-rounded current-price totals. FY2026-27 defence spending is a Budget Estimate, not actual expenditure.

pages.label: 17 / DEFENCE EXPORTS AND IMPORTS
pages.title: Defence exports rose sharply.
pages.deck: Selling more abroad and buying major weapons abroad can happen together.
blocks: The latest export value is about 56 times the 2013-14 figure. That means an increase of about 5,501%, using the earlier value as the starting base. It rose about 62.7% from 2024-25. These are rupee export values, not the number of weapons exported.

In 2025-26, public-sector defence companies exported Rs 21,071 crore and private companies Rs 17,353 crore: about 55% and 45% respectively. The ministry reports 145 exporters and destinations in more than 80 countries. These counts show reach, not profit or wholly Indian content.

The Matrix chart's 700-to-38,424 comparison is close to the official rounded-baseline story. The exact historical figure is 686. Its percentage method divides the increase by the later total. That answers a different arithmetic question from growth, which divides by the earlier total.

For a simple example, 100 becoming 200 is 100% growth. The added 100 is also 50% of the later 200. Neither calculation tells us that a government caused that percentage of the result. Dates and a subtraction cannot separate policy effects from other influences.

The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, or SIPRI, places India second among major-arms importers in its March 2026 report. India had 8.2% of global imports in 2021-25. That is its share of the world import market, not the share of its own equipment imported. Its import volume fell 4% against 2016-20.

SIPRI measures major-arms transfer volume using its own indicator; the ministry measures exports in money. The two cannot be divided to calculate a self-reliance percentage. Both sources show why the report card needs export growth and continuing import dependence on the same page.
pages.note: The four Matrix rows covered here are steel (p10), coal (p11), startups (p14) and defence exports (p20). Full cross-chart checks continue in Part 6.

pages.label: A NOTE FROM THE AUTHOR
pages.title: The numbers touch real lives.
pages.deck: Safety, justice, clean air and water belong in the same report card.
blocks: A road can get wider while the number of people dying on it rises. A court can put its records online while cases keep waiting. A city can have cleaner air than before and still have air that falls short of the standard. I wanted this part to explain those situations without making you fight through a pile of official language.

I write on MisterLove because I like taking a difficult subject apart until its meaning becomes clear. My work moves between research, business and technology. In this volume, the most useful question is often a small one: does this number count people, cases, places, capacity or something else?

The Matrix India posts started the series. The tribal-crime chart is one I return to here. I checked its entries against the original NCRB table, included the places it left out and explained why an empty rate cannot be turned into zero.

This is a before-and-after report, with 2014 as the organising point. It is not a claim that every change came from one government. Reporting rules, population, state administration, courts, communities and long-running programmes all belong in the explanation.

I also do not want an old observation to pass as a new one. A report released in 2026 can describe crimes in 2024 or emissions in 2022. Where I could not find a fair pre-2014 comparison, I say so and use the available dated comparison.

Start with the subject you care about. The table gives the numbers. The paragraphs explain each row, then show what remains unanswered. You should not need a degree, a political loyalty or a love of long reports to follow it.

pages.label: YOUR READING MAP
pages.title: A number needs a meaning.
pages.deck: The date, the unit and the coverage are part of the number.
blocks: Crime totals, murder, women, children and caste-based atrocities
All 36 states and Union Territories in the tribal-crime table
Police, court delays, prisons, information rights and voting
Air, forest cover, greenhouse gases and climate
Rivers, groundwater, waste, tigers and wetlands
Numbered sources; click a title to open the publication

One lakh means 100,000. One crore means 10 million. A rate per lakh compares a count with a population of 100,000. If a place has 20 recorded cases among two lakh people, its rate is 10 per lakh. A case is not necessarily one victim.

A percentage point is the gap between two percentages. Going from 60% to 70% adds 10 points. It is about 16.7% growth compared with the earlier 60. A rate and a growth percentage answer different questions.

FY means financial year, April to March. Calendar-year crime totals cover January to December. Court and prison figures often count the stock on one date. A stock of pending cases cannot be added to annual new cases as if they were separate events.

The research cut-off is 3 October 2026. This part covers the main national measures in these subjects and the supplied tribal-crime chart. Parts 1-4 cover the economy, infrastructure, living conditions and production. Part 6 will examine international rankings, state differences and the wider chart audit.
pages.note: Latest means the latest observation verified for that measure, not a completed statistical account of every day in 2026.

pages.label: 01 / RECORDED CRIME
pages.title: The total changed. So did the rules.
pages.deck: Police records count registered cases, not every offence that happened.
blocks: Cognisable means the kind of offence for which police can normally investigate without first obtaining a magistrate's order. IPC is the old Indian Penal Code. BNS, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, replaced it from 1 July 2024. Special and Local Laws include offences under separate central or state laws.

The first row is the main criminal code. The second is the other laws collected in this report. The third adds those two groups. Do not add the total again. The later calendar year combines IPC cases from the earlier part of 2024 with BNS cases from the later part.

NCRB also changed its collection. It excluded the heads for simple hurt under IPC Section 323, food and drug adulteration under Sections 272-276, and criminal intimidation under Section 506. Other forms of hurt remain. A lower total therefore cannot be read as a clean measurement of less actual crime.

One FIR can contain several offences. NCRB's principal-offence rule usually counts it under the most serious offence. An FIR is the police's First Information Report; it is not a court finding that somebody is guilty.

For IPC/BNS cases, the 2024 conviction rate is 53.3%. Its denominator is cases in which trial was completed, not all complaints or all registered cases. Cases still waiting for trial are outside that calculation. Reporting, investigation and judgment are different stages.
pages.note: Definitions and collection changes are in the report itself. More registration can reflect better reporting as well as more offences.

pages.label: 02 / MURDER
pages.title: Fewer registered murder cases.
pages.deck: A case count and a population rate tell two parts of the story.
blocks: The 2024 count is 6,152 lower than in 2013, a fall of about 18.5%. In plain terms, an earlier count of 100 became about 81. The count also fell by 672 between 2023 and 2024, about 2.4%.

The rate adjusts for the size of the population. The reported rate fell from 2.7 to 1.9 cases per 100,000 people. Those published rates are rounded. They help distinguish a change in the number of cases from a change relative to the number of people.

These are murder cases registered by police. A single case can involve more than one person killed. In 2013, NCRB separately reported 33,901 murder victims; replacing the earlier case count with that victim count would mix two units.

NCRB records disputes as the most common stated motive in 2024, in 9,607 cases. Personal vendetta or enmity accounted for 3,638; gain for 1,460. These are police classifications of cases, not a complete psychological explanation of every killing.

This is a clear decline in the registered murder series. It does not mean violence of every kind fell by 18.5%, or that every district became safer. Assault, domestic abuse, sexual violence and offences never registered need their own evidence.

A national rate also spreads very different local experiences into one average. Someone living in a district facing violence can face a worse situation even when the country's total falls. The table describes the countrywide record, not a promise about an individual's safety.
pages.note: Cases, victims and accused persons are separate units. Population rates here use NCRB population estimates for the stated years.

pages.label: 03 / WOMEN AND SEXUAL VIOLENCE
pages.title: Different offences moved differently.
pages.deck: Read the whole category and the rape row separately.
blocks: The first row covers several offences against women. It rose by about 42.6%. The second compares those cases with the female population: about 52 cases per lakh women became about 65. This rate is not calculated using all men and women together.

The rape row fell by about 12.4% in the registered-case series. The cruelty row remained around 1.2 lakh cases. A fall in rape cases and a rise in the wider category can both occur, because the wider category includes many other offences.

The latest all-crime count is below 2023's 4,48,211. That one-year fall does not erase the longer-period rise. Likewise, the long-period rise does not tell us that registration increased in every intervening year.

The law changed around this baseline. The 2013 criminal-law amendment broadened sexual-offence provisions, and POCSO introduced a separate framework for children. Legal definitions, willingness to complain and police recording affect comparisons across time.

The figures leave out violence that never becomes a registered case. They cannot establish that an unreported assault did not happen. They also cannot tell us how much of a rise came from more violence and how much from more reporting.

A police complaint is not proof of guilt. An acquittal is not, by itself, proof that the complaint was invented. Investigation and the evidence required in court determine the outcome. The table is useful precisely when we keep those different questions apart.
pages.note: Women and child categories overlap; adding them would double-count some cases. These are registered cases, not a victimisation survey.

pages.label: 04 / CHILDREN
pages.title: Much more crime is being recorded.
pages.deck: The category grew, with kidnapping and POCSO cases making up large shares.
blocks: Children means people below 18 in this report. The all-crime count is about 3.22 times the 2013 count. The rate is also higher, so population growth alone does not explain the larger recorded category.

The last two rows break down 2024. Kidnapping and abduction made up about 40% of recorded child-crime cases. POCSO made up about 36.9%. POCSO means Protection of Children from Sexual Offences. These rows are parts of the total, not extra cases to add to it.

The POCSO law began in 2012, close to the earlier comparison point. The legal framework and the detail collected expanded over the longer period. The rise cannot honestly be turned into a claim that the same narrowly defined risk became exactly 3.22 times greater.

A registered kidnapping category also needs the case's facts. It cannot be read as a count of children kidnapped by strangers alone. The statistical label does not describe who the accused was or what happened in every case.

The total rose from 1,77,335 in 2023 to 1,87,702 in 2024, about 5.8%. This is a continuing rise in the latest registered total. It deserves attention even while definitions and reporting are kept in view.

Girls can appear in both the women and children chapters. One event may therefore be described in more than one victim-group table. Those chapters help us understand different groups; they are not separate piles that can all be added to calculate a new national crime total.
pages.note: A dash in the 2013 breakdown means no matched figure is supplied here. It does not mean zero offences occurred.

pages.label: 05 / CASTE AND TRIBAL ATROCITIES
pages.title: The national totals need context.
pages.deck: The tribal-crime chart is about a specific recorded category.
blocks: Scheduled Castes, or SCs, and Scheduled Tribes, or STs, are legally recognised groups. The later SC count is about 41.3% above 2013. The later ST count is about 46.7% above 2013. Both are lower than their 2023 counts.

The recent tables concern crimes and atrocities against these groups within NCRB's stated scope. The ST table says atrocities concern offences committed against STs by non-SC/ST persons. It excludes IPC-only cases without the SC/ST Act where the offender is from SC/ST groups. It is not a count of every crime involving a tribal person.

The legal framework and reporting coverage changed over the long comparison, including amendments to the atrocities law. These before-and-after totals should not be treated as an unchanged survey of all violence, discrimination or actual risk.

The published 2024 rates are 27.7 per lakh SC people and 9.5 per lakh ST people. Their denominators still come from the 2011 Census. They are not rates calculated from a fresh 2024 or 2026 count of those populations.

The ST national total fell by 2,994 from 2023 to 2024. Manipur alone fell from 3,399 to 289, a reduction of 3,110. Across the remaining places together, the net change was an increase of 116. This arithmetic shows how much one state's swing shaped the national change.
It does not tell us why that swing occurred. The next two pages reproduce all 36 places in the official table, sorted by published 2024 rate, and explain the errors in the supplied chart.
pages.note: The rate is specific to the SC or ST population. The 2011 denominator and legal scope are essential parts of the comparison.

pages.label: 06 / TRIBAL CRIME: ALL 36 PLACES
pages.title: Tribal crime, place by place.
pages.deck: Registered cases by year. Rate means cases per lakh ST people in 2024.
blocks: Kerala has the highest published rate, 29.9, with 145 cases. Madhya Pradesh has the largest count, 3,165, with a rate of 20.7. A smaller population can produce a higher rate from fewer cases. These are recorded rates in this specific category, using ST population from the 2011 Census. They are not a ranking of every kind of danger faced by tribal people.
pages.note: Sorted by the published 2024 rate, highest first. Rounded rates should not be recalculated from the table's rounded population figures.

pages.label: 07 / TRIBAL CRIME: CONTINUED
pages.title: The rest of the same table.
pages.deck: An unpublished rate stays unpublished. It is different from a recorded zero.
blocks: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu

The supplied chart gives Punjab a rate of 0.2. NCRB prints no rate. It also prints no rate for Chandigarh and Puducherry, where the chart shows zero. Haryana and Delhi are missing from that chart; both appear here. The five 'No rate' places have no notified ST population denominator in the cited Census table. Their recorded cases remain visible.
pages.note: A recorded zero does not establish absence of unreported violence. This category and its legal scope are explained on page 8. All 36 places are included.

pages.label: 08 / CYBERCRIME
pages.title: The recorded count rose sharply.
pages.deck: A growing digital economy also gives crime more digital routes.
blocks: The two 2013 rows add to 5,693. The Information Technology Act covers specified digital offences; some cyber-enabled offences were counted under IPC. The 2024 total is about 18 times that combined earlier count. It rose about 17.9% from 2023.

That large increase is in registered cases. The newer framework collects a broader range of offences, while digital use and opportunities to report have also expanded. Dividing the totals alone cannot show that the risk for each internet user rose 18 times.

Fraud was the recorded motive in 73,987 cases in 2024, or 72.6% of the cybercrime total. A motive category is not the amount of money lost. One case can involve several victims, and a complaint to an online portal is not automatically a police FIR.

The government says its financial-fraud response system saved more than Rs 11,158 crore across over 32.80 lakh complaints by 30 June 2026. These are cumulative figures for the system launched in 2021. They are not the number of 2024 FIRs, an annual loss estimate or proof that all the money reached victims again.

For someone facing an online financial fraud, 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in are the official reporting routes. Prompt reporting helps the response system try to stop funds moving further. The larger report-card question is whether prevention, investigation and recovery keep pace with the growth in recorded fraud.
pages.note: NCRB case counts and the cybercrime portal's cumulative complaints use different units and cannot be added.

pages.label: 09 / ROAD SAFETY
pages.title: Similar crashes. More deaths.
pages.deck: The long-term rise in deaths is much larger than the rise in reported crashes.
blocks: Reported crashes rose by about 0.3% between these years. Deaths rose by 39,603, or about 28.8%. The injury count was lower. These rows count different things: an event, people killed and people injured.

The last row divides deaths by reported crashes. It went from about 28 deaths per 100 crashes to about 36. This does not mean each crash has a 36% chance of killing someone. One crash can kill several people. It is a measure of the seriousness of the reported crash record.

Deaths also rose from 1,72,890 in 2023 to 1,77,175 in 2024, about 2.5%. The latest year therefore continued the recent rise. A longer or wider road network has not automatically delivered fewer road deaths.

More vehicles and more travel change exposure. A per-kilometre risk calculation would need the distance travelled, not only these totals. The annual deaths remain important even without that calculation: they measure lives lost.

Road design, speeds, vehicle protection, enforcement and emergency care can all influence the outcome. This table cannot allocate the increase between those causes. Nor can it show that every highway or state moved in the same direction.

This page keeps the ministry's historical series together. NCRB has a separate road-death total of 1,75,142 for 2024. Different reporting systems can produce different totals. Adding those two counts would largely count the same deaths twice.
pages.note: MoRTH = Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. All main rows use its series, rather than switching sources between endpoints.

pages.label: 10 / SUICIDES
pages.title: The long-term count is higher.
pages.deck: The latest small fall follows several years of rising recorded deaths.
blocks: The 2024 count is 35,947 above 2013, about 26.7% higher. The reported population rate is also higher, from 11.0 to 12.2 per lakh. More people in the country do not explain the whole increase in the recorded rate.
The 2019 row shows why two endpoints do not tell the entire path. Its count was slightly above 2013, but its rate was lower. Recorded deaths then rose substantially before the latest small fall.
Between 2023 and 2024, the count fell by 672, about 0.4%. That is a change in the latest year, not a reversal of the full rise since 2013. Both facts belong on the page.

NCRB compiles suicides reported to police. These are not counts from a complete clinical survey of mental health. Differences in recognition and reporting affect the record; the figures do not cover every unrecorded death.

The report lists stated causes and occupations. A police-recorded cause is not a medical diagnosis or a complete account of a person's life. Several pressures can exist together. An occupation category says what work the person did, not that the occupation itself caused the death.

These numbers describe a serious loss of life. They support looking closely at prevention, accessible care and social pressures. They do not support blaming every death on a single policy, exam, occupation or personal failing.
pages.note: No methods of suicide are described. The earlier count and rate are confirmed in the parliamentary annexure; later values use ADSI 2024.

pages.label: 11 / POLICE CAPACITY
pages.title: More personnel. Many vacancies.
pages.deck: A sanctioned post is permission to employ someone; an actual post is filled.
blocks: The number of personnel actually serving rose by 4,39,650, about 25.5%. The approved establishment also grew. The first row is the intended staffing ceiling; it does not mean all those officers were already working.

Subtracting actual staff from sanctioned staff gives the vacancy count. The later shortfall is 31,978 larger in absolute numbers, but smaller as a share of the expanded establishment: about 21.5% instead of 24.6%. Both statements can be true.

Using the report's projected population, the 2024 actual strength is about 155 personnel per lakh people. This includes civil police, District Armed Reserve, Special Armed Police and India Reserve Battalions in the state and UT establishment. Central forces are reported separately.

Women numbered 2,72,535 in that establishment, about 12.6% of its actual strength. A national share does not show whether every station has enough women, whether they hold leadership positions or which duties they are assigned.

This publication describes 1 January 2024, although it was published in 2025. It is not a live count of staff in October 2026. Police and public order are primarily state responsibilities, so staffing differs widely between states.

Staff numbers are one part of capacity. Training, time spent on other duties, investigation skills, equipment and the ability to register a complaint also matter. A larger force alone cannot tell us whether an investigation was fair or finished promptly.
pages.note: Percentages are calculated from the cited sanctioned and actual totals. The comparison excludes central-force totals from both sides.

pages.label: 12 / COURTS AND DELAY
pages.title: Many more cases are waiting.
pages.deck: Digital access expanded while the stock of pending cases grew.
blocks: High Court pendency rose by about 44.9%. District and subordinate court pendency rose by about 86%. These are stocks of cases awaiting disposal on the two dates. They are not the number newly filed in each year.

The Supreme Court had another 95,954 pending cases in the July 2026 snapshot. Adding the three levels gives 5,64,74,844, about 5.65 crore. No matched 2013 Supreme Court figure is inserted into the table, so it does not pretend to offer an all-level 2013 comparison.

The queue can grow even when courts dispose of many cases, if incoming cases outnumber completed ones. Disposal is a flow over time; pendency is the stock left at a date. A pending case is also not necessarily a criminal case: these totals include different kinds of disputes.

The August 2026 reply reports more than 4.18 crore video hearings, about 1.25 crore electronic filings and 2,584 eSewa centres. These are cumulative service figures. A hearing is not a separate completed case, and several hearings can concern the same case.

At 30 June 2026, the reply records 21,411 working district/subordinate judicial officers against 30,825 sanctioned posts. That gap is another part of the capacity picture. Courtrooms, staffing and case management need to be considered together.

Online filing and access can save journeys and make a case easier to track. They do not prove that waiting times disappeared. To measure speed directly, we need the age and duration of cases as well as the number pending.
pages.note: Latest pendency is the dated parliamentary NJDG snapshot. It is not a claim to be the live dashboard reading on 3 October 2026.

pages.label: 13 / PRISONS AND UNDERTRIALS
pages.title: Prisons remain over capacity.
pages.deck: Most people in prison are undertrials, awaiting the outcome of proceedings.
blocks: Capacity is the number of people the prison system is designed to hold. It grew by about 30.4%. The number held grew by about 23.5%. Capacity grew faster, so national occupancy fell, but it remained above 100%.
An occupancy rate of 112.2% means roughly 112 people for every 100 places. It does not mean every prison has exactly that crowding. Some are below capacity; others face much greater pressure.

The 2024 values come from NCRB's revision dated 15 September 2026. They count 5,09,012 people. Earlier published 2024 figures quoted elsewhere can differ. This page uses the revised counts and their matching occupancy rate together.

Undertrial prisoners are held while proceedings are ongoing; they have not been convicted in the case for which they are held as undertrials. Their share rose from 67.6% to 72.5%, or 4.9 percentage points. Prison population must not be described as a count of convicted offenders.
The other categories include convicts and people detained under other legal provisions. The undertrial row is part of the total, so adding it to the inmate count would double-count people.
These are year-end snapshots. They do not count everyone admitted over the entire year, and they cannot alone measure sentence length, bail access or conditions inside a particular jail.
pages.note: The 2024 report was revised in 2026; its observation remains 31 December 2024. Undertrial status is not a finding of guilt.

pages.label: 14 / INFORMATION RIGHTS AND VOTING
pages.title: Two ways citizens take part.
pages.deck: Requesting public information and casting a vote need different measures.
blocks: RTI means Right to Information. The Act, passed in 2005, lets people request information from public authorities. The cited rejection rate concerns the Union authorities reporting through the central system. It is not the combined rate for every state authority.

The rejection rate fell by 3.95 percentage points. But an application not rejected is not necessarily a complete, useful answer. The February 2026 reply says separate data on partially answered or unresolved applications are not collected.

The Central Information Commission had 29,034 appeals and 3,577 complaints pending on 1 February 2026. Those are different types of pending matters, not the annual number of RTI applications. A low initial rejection rate can coexist with a queue of disputes.

Turnout is votes cast as a share of registered electors. The Election Commission's atlas shows 58.21% in 2009, 66.44% in 2014, 67.40% in 2019 and 66.10% in 2024. The latest share is above 2009 but below the previous two general elections.

The 2014 election belongs to the transition year, so the table uses 2009 as its pre-2014 observation. The atlas's total includes the final voting record; an earlier polling-day percentage should not replace it without saying the coverage changed.

Participation, access to information, case delays and police capacity each describe one part of institutions. None of these figures is a complete democracy or corruption score. International indices and their methods are examined separately in Part 6.
pages.note: RTI uses financial years; voting uses the named general election. Turnout is not a share of all residents, because only registered electors form its denominator.

pages.label: 15 / AIR QUALITY
pages.title: Improvement is not the finish line.
pages.deck: A city can reduce pollution and still fail an air-quality standard.
blocks: NCAP is the National Clean Air Programme, launched in 2019. Its comparison uses 2017-18, not 2014. These results describe its 130 cities, not a national average weighted by how many people breathe each city's air.

PM10 is airborne particulate matter up to 10 micrometres across; PM2.5 is the smaller fraction up to 2.5. Their annual averages are measured in micrograms per cubic metre of air. PM2.5 is part of PM10, so the two concentrations should not be added.
The 72 cities with reductions above 20% and the 26 above 40% sit within the 108 improved cities. These groups overlap. Adding 108, 72 and 26 would count many cities repeatedly.

Only 14 met India's annual PM10 limit of 60, compared with six in the baseline year. The annual PM2.5 limit is 40. WHO's 2021 health-based annual guidelines are lower: 15 for PM10 and 5 for PM2.5, in the same units.

For example, the reply gives Delhi an annual PM2.5 value of 102 in 2025-26. That is above both benchmarks. Mumbai's reported value is 33: below India's annual limit but above WHO's guideline. Meeting the Indian standard and meeting the WHO guideline are different results.

An annual average can also hide very polluted days. The count of cities that improved answers whether measured conditions changed against the programme baseline. The standards answer a separate question about the level that remains.
pages.note: No matched pre-2014 all-India PM average is invented. Programme results and standards are kept separate; lower pollution is not the same as no pollution.

pages.label: 16 / FORESTS AND TREES
pages.title: More cover. Uneven changes.
pages.deck: The matched national comparison includes gains outside recorded forest areas.
blocks: FSI, the Forest Survey of India, recomputed the earlier figures for a matched comparison in the 2023 report. Its original 2013 headline was different. Using the revised baseline with the revised endpoint avoids treating a mapping revision as new tree growth.

Forest cover rose by 16,630.25 square kilometres, about 2.38%. Separately measured tree cover rose by 20,747.34, about 22.73%. The combined increase was 37,377.59, or about 4.73%. The combined row already contains the first two.

Forest cover means patches larger than one hectare with at least 10% tree canopy, regardless of ownership, legal status or land use. It includes some orchards and plantations. Tree cover separately measures other tree patches and dispersed trees. More mapped cover is not automatically more old natural forest.

Inside recorded forest areas, the matched forest-cover increase was only 440.47 square kilometres. Outside them it was 16,189.78. Most of the net mapped increase was therefore outside recorded areas. That location alone does not establish the kind or ecological quality of every new patch.

The North-East row is part of the national forest total, not extra cover. Across its eight states, cover fell by 3,132.27 square kilometres. A national increase therefore coexists with a substantial regional loss.

The latest assessment puts combined forest and tree cover at 25.17% of India's land area. This is the 2023 assessment, using imagery from earlier observation periods. It is not a measurement of all forests in October 2026.
pages.note: Use Chapter 9 for the matched historical figures. Cover, legal forest area, natural-forest quality and biodiversity are distinct measures.

pages.label: 17 / GREENHOUSE GASES
pages.title: More emissions. Lower intensity.
pages.deck: The total and the amount per unit of economic output can move differently.
blocks: GHG emissions excluding land use, million tonnes CO2-equivalent
Emissions per unit of GDP: index

GHG means greenhouse gases, including carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide. CO2-equivalent puts their different warming effects into a common unit. These gases are different from the local particle-pollution measure on page 18.

India's first Biennial Transparency Report, submitted in April 2026, puts emissions excluding land use and forestry about 69.7% above 2005 by 2022. The inventory's latest year is 2022. A 2026 submission is not a 2026 emissions observation.

Intensity means emissions per unit of economic output. It fell by 37.38%, so an earlier index of 100 became 62.62. If output doubles while emissions rise by half, the emissions per unit fall by 25%. A growing total and a falling intensity can therefore both be true.

The official climate-pledge baseline is 2005, not 2014. The matched inventory does not provide a 2013 entry. Forests and other land uses remove part of the emissions; including those removals, net national emissions still rose by 57.33% from 2005 to 2022.

The July 2026 reply reports non-fossil electricity capacity at 54.18% on 30 June. Capacity is equipment installed, not its share of electricity actually generated. The intensity-reduction target is 45% by 2030 and 47% by 2035; those targets are future commitments.

The same reply reports an additional forest-and-tree carbon sink of 2.44 billion tonnes of CO2-equivalent from 2005 to 2022. That is additional stored carbon, not an annual quantity that can simply be subtracted from one year's emissions.
pages.note: The first row uses report-rounded values; the stated changes use the inventory calculations. Targets, installed capacity, carbon stocks and annual emissions are separate.

pages.label: 18 / HEAT AND CLIMATE
pages.title: One cooler year does not end warming.
pages.deck: Compare temperatures against the same long-term reference.
blocks: IMD, the India Meteorological Department, compares these years with India's average annual temperature over 1991-2020. The value 0.65 C is a gap above that reference. It is not an outdoor temperature of 65 degrees, or an increase measured only since 2014.

The 2009 observation gives earlier context using the same reference in the latest statement. A matched 2013 value was not verified here, so none is invented. One earlier year's temperature is also not a substitute for a long-term average.

2024 was warmer than 2025 in this measure. Yet 2025 was still the eighth-warmest year in India's record beginning in 1901. Annual temperatures fluctuate; one lower reading does not erase a longer trend.

The 2016-2025 decade was the warmest recorded decade, 0.32 C above the same reference. Across 1901-2025, the reported mean-temperature trend is 0.68 C per 100 years. That is the trend's rate, not a claim that warming began in 2014.

IMD reports 1,274 millimetres of rain in 2025, 110% of the 1971-2020 annual normal. A millimetre measures the depth of rain; 110% means about 10% more than that reference amount. Rainfall uses its own stated baseline, not the temperature baseline.

An annual national average does not tell us where rain fell or whether it arrived in damaging bursts. Heat, floods and drought are local experiences shaped by weather, buildings, land use and preparedness. A warming trend and better disaster protection are different questions, so neither should stand in for the other.
pages.note: All temperature entries share the 1991-2020 reference. Rainfall uses the report's 1971-2020 normal. Observations stop at 2025.

pages.label: 19 / RIVERS AND SEWAGE
pages.title: Fewer listed polluted stretches.
pages.deck: The latest river list uses earlier monitoring and a specific pollution test.
blocks: A stretch is a section of a river. One river can have more than one polluted stretch. That is why 296 stretches and 271 affected rivers are different counts, and why neither means all 623 rivers were polluted.

The listed stretch count fell by 55, about 15.7%, against the 2018 report. The 2025 assessment uses water-quality monitoring from 2022-23. Its name is the report year, not a claim that every sample was taken in 2025.

CPCB, the Central Pollution Control Board, identifies these stretches mainly through BOD, biochemical oxygen demand. It measures the oxygen used as microbes break down organic matter. A value above 3 milligrams per litre is the assessment criterion used here.

High BOD can leave less oxygen for aquatic life. Low BOD alone does not prove that water is safe to drink: microbes, metals and other contaminants require their own tests. This list is therefore not a complete map of every kind of water pollution.

Monitoring coverage and stretch boundaries change. The 15.7% fall is a change in the published list, not proof that pollution in every Indian river fell by that percentage. A fair matched pre-2014 nationwide stretch comparison is not supplied here.

Namami Gange created 4,263 million litres per day of sewage-treatment capacity by June 2026. That is potential daily treatment, not the verified volume treated every day. Whether sewage reaches the plant, the plant runs properly and its output meets standards determines the actual benefit.
pages.note: Latest polluted-stretch counts follow the main assessment tables and the March 2026 parliamentary confirmation. Treatment capacity is kept separate from river-water quality.

pages.label: 20 / GROUNDWATER
pages.title: The average hides local pressure.
pages.deck: The amount taken out must be compared with the resource assessed as available.
blocks: Recharge is water replenishing the underground resource. The second row is what the assessment counts as available for use after its deductions. Withdrawal is water taken out. A billion cubic metres is one billion units of 1,000 litres each.

The old headline stage was about 62%; the 2025 stage is 60.63%. It does not mean 60.63% of all underground water has been used up. It compares estimated annual withdrawal with the assessed annual extractable resource.

The 2025 share is lower than the 2013 headline, but slightly above 2024's 60.47%. The most recent change was an increase of 0.16 percentage points. Keeping both comparisons avoids presenting every year as an improvement.

Over-exploited means extraction exceeds the annual resource under the assessment. The share of units so classified fell from about 15.70% to 10.80%. But boundaries, the number of units and assessment methods changed, so this is not an unchanged panel of identical local areas.

In 2025, over-exploited and critical units made up more than a quarter of units in Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Delhi and Tamil Nadu. A manageable-looking national average cannot make a stressed local aquifer safe.

These are estimates, not readings from one giant national underground tank. Rain, recharge, irrigation demand and measurement changes affect them. Water level and water quality also need local evidence.
pages.note: The 2013 assessment was published in 2017; the 2025 assessment was released in November 2025. Historical methods and availability definitions differ.

pages.label: 21 / URBAN WASTE
pages.title: Much more waste is reported processed.
pages.deck: Collection, processing and recycling describe different steps.
blocks: The June 2026 government backgrounder reports processing rising from 16% to 82%. That is a gain of 66 percentage points. In the programme's reported waste measure, roughly 16 out of 100 became 82 out of 100.

Collection coverage rose from 43% to 98%, a gain of 55 points. This is the reported urban service indicator. The backgrounder does not spell out its full counting base, so I do not turn it into a claim about 98% of all Indian households.

Collection is getting waste from the point where it is discarded. Processing is handling it through a treatment route. Recycling is recovering material for use again. Waste counted as processed can go through composting, biological treatment, fuel production or other routes; 82% processed does not mean 82% recycled.

The January 2026 ministry reply gave 81.30% processing in its dated administrative record. The June backgrounder reports 82%. Different dates and rounding matter. Neither is presented here as a new October survey.

These are official administrative results, based on programme reporting. They are useful for tracking the reported expansion of services. They do not establish that every collection round happened, that every plant met its standards or that every city performed equally.

New daily waste is a flow. Old waste accumulated in dumps is a stock. A high share of fresh waste processed does not mean every old landfill has been cleared. Cleaner streets, properly treated waste and restored dumpsites require separate evidence.
pages.note: Urban programme coverage is not all-India rural-and-urban household coverage. Processing and recycling should not be used as interchangeable words.

pages.label: 22 / TIGERS AND WETLANDS
pages.title: Recovery and recognition grew.
pages.deck: Animal estimates and protected-site designations are different kinds of progress.
blocks: The estimated tiger population rose by about 65.4% from 2014 to 2022. The earlier census belongs to the transition year, not a fully pre-2014 year. The latest estimation verified in the July 2026 update still describes 2022.

The final 2022 estimate is 3,682. The earlier minimum estimate of 3,167 covered camera-trapped areas; further analysis included other tiger-presence areas. Those are two stages of the same estimation, not two different annual populations.

This is a scientific estimate using field work, camera traps and modelling. It is not an exact headcount of every tiger alive on the day of publication. The final report also gives an upper estimate of 3,925.

The reserve network expanded from 46 to 58. More reserves mean more sites designated for tiger conservation; the count alone does not describe their size, condition or links between habitats. Project Tiger began in 1973, so the conservation story long predates 2014.

Ramsar sites are wetlands recognised as internationally important under the Convention on Wetlands. The count reached 101 with Glaw Lake in Arunachal Pradesh in August 2026. It was 26 in 2014. The increase is in recognised sites, not proof that India gained 75 entirely new wetlands.

These are substantial gains in the measured indicators. They do not establish that every species or ecosystem recovered. The tiger report describes local declines too. Water quality, habitat connections and pressure on people living around protected areas remain part of conservation.
pages.note: All three measures keep their own dates. The tiger estimate is 2022; reserve and Ramsar counts are dated 2026 updates. Part 6 follows with rankings and wider chart checks.

pages.label: A NOTE FROM THE AUTHOR
pages.title: One country. Many different lives.
pages.deck: The last part asks what the national headlines leave out.
blocks: I wanted this report to answer a simple question: what changed in India, and what do those changes mean for someone living here? A long list of impressive numbers is easy to share. Understanding which numbers belong together takes more patience.

For me, that patience matters. I write about ideas, research and public life through MisterLove. I want a reader to understand a figure without needing a degree, a party membership or a glossary beside every sentence. That is why I have kept the explanations direct.

A person can benefit from a new road and still struggle to find steady work. A state can become less poor and still have many families facing hardship. A country can build more hospitals while questions about quality, access and freedom remain. These experiences can exist together.

This final volume brings the states and international rankings into the picture. It also returns to the Matrix India charts. All 15 economic rows and all 23 rows of the supplied infrastructure chart appear with an explanation. The Scheduled Tribe crime chart's 36-place check is in Part 5; its key corrections are carried forward here.

I also examine selected consumption, growth, income, railway and defence posts from the same account. Where the underlying annual data or a clear definition could not be established, I say so. This is a report built from the identified charts and published sources, not a complete archive of everything the account has posted.

I have not given India one final mark. There is no honest arithmetic that turns roads, hunger, jobs and civil rights into a single grade without choosing whose needs count more. I would rather show the evidence clearly and let you form a view with the facts in front of you.
pages.note: Research frozen at 3 October 2026. A report published in 2026 may describe an earlier year. Missing comparisons remain missing.
