Parts 1 to 5 cover the economy; infrastructure; health and education; farming, industry, science and defence; and crime, institutions and the environment. Their tables explain the underlying national figures in more detail. This part adds the comparisons and chart checks.

A financial year such as 2025-26 runs from April 2025 to March 2026. A survey period such as 2019-21 covers fieldwork across those years. An estimate can be revised. A forecast describes what may happen. These labels change the meaning of the number.
pages.note: The six volumes total 168 pages: 28 + 28 + 32 + 24 + 28 + 28. Page references in this map refer to Part 6.

pages.label: 01 / RANK AND SCORE
pages.title: A rank is a place in a queue.
pages.deck: A score tells you more about what was measured.
blocks: Imagine three runners. You finish a race in 12 minutes, then improve to 11 minutes next year. If two other runners improve even more, you can move from second to third while running faster. A country's rank works like that: it depends on everyone else too.

A score is the measured result under an index's rules. A rank sorts those scores. Being 100th does not mean scoring 100 points. A rank of 100 among 120 countries also differs from 100 among 190. Always keep the number of countries beside the rank.

The direction matters. Higher HDI and corruption-perception scores are better. Lower hunger scores are better. Rank 1 normally leads the list. Old press-freedom scores used the opposite direction from today's scale, so comparing their raw values would reverse the meaning.

Methods matter as well. Adding an indicator, changing a weight or improving a data source can move a score without an equally large change in everyday conditions. Where possible, use a single report's recalculated history. That applies the same framework to the earlier and later years.

A report's year is another label, not an observation date. India's latest HDI in this report was published in 2025 and describes 2023. Happiness in the 2026 edition averages 2023-2025. Writing all of those as 'India today' would hide the delay.

Finally, ask who publishes the index. UNDP, the World Bank, a research network and a civil-society organisation have different mandates and methods. Naming the publisher lets you assess its choices. A ranking is useful evidence about its subject; it is not a measurement of every part of India.

The following pages therefore keep the publisher, date, score where verified, country coverage and comparison limit together. No rank is turned into a percentage of Indians who are happy, honest, hungry or free.
pages.note: Examples explain the arithmetic; they are not estimates of Indian conditions. The latest verified edition is used at the stated research cutoff.

pages.label: 02 / DIFFERENCES BETWEEN STATES
pages.title: The national average hides a lot.
pages.deck: Start with income, then look at poverty and development together.
blocks: These are RBI's per capita net state domestic product figures at each year's prices, from its 2024-25 handbook. They are annual averages, not wages. Inflation is included. Delhi's later figure is about seven times Bihar's; it does not mean every Delhi resident earns seven times every Bihar resident.

The next two pages show all 28 states and eight union territories. MPI means multidimensional poverty: overlapping shortages in health, education and living conditions. A resident counts as poor here if their household faces at least one-third of the weighted deprivations across 12 indicators.

India's MPI headcount fell from 24.85% in 2015-16 to 14.96% in 2019-21. That is a fall of 9.89 percentage points. These survey dates are both after 2014; this is not a 2014-to-2026 comparison. Rural figures fell from 32.59% to 19.28%; urban figures from 8.65% to 5.27%.

The last column is NITI's SDG India Index score for 2023-24. Higher means closer to the chosen development targets; lower MPI means fewer residents meet the poverty definition. The columns have different dates and methods. They should not be added into a personal mark for a state.
pages.note: Income uses a common FY2024-25 snapshot, not the latest economic survey of every state. The poverty table uses survey observations, not later projected poverty estimates.

pages.label: 03 / ALL STATES AND UNION TERRITORIES
pages.title: Where the state figures stand.
pages.deck: Sorted by the 2019-21 poverty share, from lower to higher.
blocks: Read Kerala's 0.55 as about 0.55 residents in every 100 meeting this poverty definition in the survey. It is not a claim that nobody there struggles. An SDG score of 79 is a composite result, not 79% of residents being wealthy.
pages.note: UT means union territory. MPI is a resident headcount share; SDG is a 0-100 index. Current geographic units follow the reports, including retrospective split/merged-unit baselines. This ordering is not an overall state ranking.

pages.label: 04 / ALL STATES AND UNION TERRITORIES
pages.title: The state table, continued.
pages.deck: Sorted by the 2019-21 poverty share, from lower to higher.
blocks: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu (UT)

Bihar's poverty share fell by 18.13 points but remained 33.76%. A large improvement and a high remaining burden can both be true. The national SDG score was 71; Kerala and Uttarakhand scored 79, while Bihar scored 57.
pages.note: UT means union territory. MPI is a resident headcount share; SDG is a 0-100 index. Current geographic units follow the reports, including retrospective split/merged-unit baselines. This ordering is not an overall state ranking.

pages.label: 05 / HUMAN DEVELOPMENT
pages.title: A longer, better-equipped life.
pages.deck: UNDP combines health, schooling and income in the HDI.
blocks: HDI means Human Development Index. It combines life expectancy, expected and completed schooling, and income per person adjusted for differences in purchasing power. Its scale runs from 0 to 1. Higher is better. It asks whether people have more scope to live, learn and support themselves.

The two published scores above are different statistical vintages. UNDP revises data and historical estimates. Subtracting 0.554 from 0.685 would treat those revisions as if all of them were new progress. Use a matched series for the change over time.

Within that series, HDI rose by 0.070, about 11.4% of its earlier value. This is an index change; it does not mean every person's life improved by 11.4%. India remains in UNDP's medium human-development category in the latest assessment.

The 2023 components include life expectancy of about 72 years, expected schooling of 13 years and average completed schooling of 6.9 years for adults. Expected schooling concerns a child entering education; completed schooling concerns adults. The two figures answer different questions.

HDI is an average. UNDP's inequality-adjusted result is 0.475, about 30.7% below the headline HDI. That gap shows how uneven achievements reduce the combined measure. It is not a count of people in poverty, and it does not say which individual benefited most.
pages.note: Latest verified HDI edition: 2025, using 2023 observations. UNDP modelled life expectancy and India's domestic SRS estimate are different series; they should not be spliced.

pages.label: 06 / GENDER GAPS
pages.title: Opportunity and equality.
pages.deck: Parity is a comparison between sexes, not a measure of absolute opportunity.
blocks: The World Economic Forum compares women's and men's outcomes in economic participation, education, health and political empowerment. A score of 64.5% means that share of the measured parity gap is closed under its rules. It does not mean 64.5% of Indian women have jobs or are treated equally.

Educational parity improved strongly in these published profiles. Economic and political parity remain much lower. A country's total rank can therefore look poor even when school participation between sexes becomes more equal.

Parity is relative. If both women and men have weak access to a service, their ratio can still look equal. This index therefore does not replace the health, learning or wage levels examined in the earlier volumes. Equality and a good overall level are separate aims.

Political empowerment includes a rolling measure of years with a female head of state over the past 50 years. Older years dropping out of that window can change the score. It is not simply the proportion of women who voted or who held a local office in 2026.

The 2026 report was released on 16 September and draws on indicators from different years. Country coverage also changed. Read the scores alongside the rank: a 30-place drop is not a 30% decline in women's lives.
pages.note: Displayed scores are rounded. These are published edition comparisons, not a newly reconstructed common-indicator panel.

pages.label: 07 / HUNGER AND NUTRITION
pages.title: The hunger rank needs its history.
pages.deck: The newer method does not measure hunger in the same way as 2013.
blocks: GHI combines undernourishment, child wasting, child stunting and child mortality. Wasting means too little weight for height; stunting means too little height for age. Its score runs from 0 toward 100, with lower better. It is not the percentage of all Indians who went without dinner.

In 2013, countries with very low scores were listed separately rather than given individual ranks in the main list. The method changed in 2015, including replacing child underweight with wasting and stunting. The original 21.3 and today's 25.8 are therefore not a fair before-and-after score pair.
This matched history points to improvement, while the remaining 25.8 is still classified as serious. It does not supply a matched 2013 score. A falling score and a low international rank can coexist.

The 2025 inputs include about 12.0% undernourishment, 18.7% child wasting, 32.9% child stunting and 2.8% under-five mortality. They cover different earlier periods; wasting uses NFHS-5. They are not four 2025 surveys, and they are not meant to be added. Later NFHS-6 findings do not retroactively become inputs to this edition.

The Indian government has challenged the index's method, including the weight given to child outcomes in a population-wide label. That criticism should be read alongside the publishers' explanation. Administrative nutrition records and representative household surveys also have different coverage. Method disagreements do not make the directly measured nutrition problems disappear.
pages.note: Latest edition verified at the cutoff: 2025. Component percentages are rounded and come from the report's separate source periods. No 2026 GHI result is assumed.

pages.label: 08 / HAPPINESS
pages.title: How people rate their own lives.
pages.deck: The question concerns life as a whole, not how often someone smiles.
blocks: Respondents imagine a ladder with their worst possible life at 0 and their best possible life at 10. They say where their own life stands. The ranking sorts country averages of those answers. India's 4.536 is therefore an average assessment, not 45.36% of people being happy.

The latest average is about 0.236 points below the older one. Survey years and country coverage differ, and samples carry uncertainty. This is a descriptive comparison of two published survey windows, not proof of what one government caused.

The 2026 data give India's score a confidence interval of roughly 4.470 to 4.601. That range represents sampling uncertainty under the report's calculation. Nearby scores and ranks should not be treated as precise differences between whole populations.

The report also uses income, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom to make choices, generosity and perceived corruption to help explain country differences. Those factors are not six ingredients added together to manufacture the ranking. The ranking itself comes from people's ladder answers.

The 2025 edition put India at 118, with a score of 4.389. The 2026 edition is better on both figures. That recent improvement can exist alongside a lower score than the much earlier 2013 survey window. Choosing only one comparison can hide the other.

Country averages conceal differences by age, income, health, region and social circumstances. A low rank is not a diagnosis of depression, and a high rank does not mean nobody is lonely or struggling. For daily life, the survey is a useful extra lens beside jobs, safety, health and relationships.
pages.note: The 2026 workbook labels the latest window by its final survey year, 2025. It is not a ranking from interviews conducted only in 2026.

pages.label: 09 / INNOVATION
pages.title: More ideas reaching useful output.
pages.deck: WIPO measures the conditions for innovation and its results.
blocks: Innovation means turning knowledge and ideas into useful products, processes and services. WIPO's index brings together roughly 80 indicators. Inputs include institutions, research, skills, infrastructure and finance. Outputs include technology, knowledge and creative results.

India's position improved substantially between the published editions. In 2026, its output rank is stronger than its input rank: 25 compared with 49. That means the index places India higher for its measured results than for its measured supporting conditions.

India is first among the 36 lower-middle-income economies and first among the 11 economies in Central and Southern Asia in this edition. Those are subgroup ranks. They can coexist with being 38th overall because the overall table also includes richer economies and other regions.

The profile gives a statistical rank interval of 34 to 39. Data availability, indicators and the model can change between editions. Moving from 66 to 38 does not translate into '42% more innovative', nor does it establish the value of every invention.

India's 2026 strengths include ICT services exports, domestic market scale and later-stage venture-capital activity. Weaker relative indicators include researchers per million people, secondary pupil-teacher ratios and knowledge-intensive employment. A strong headline can therefore contain specific areas that still need work.

A patent count is another measure. Applications are requests; grants are legal approvals. Neither is automatically a successful product or a secure job. Part 4 explains patents, research spending and scientific publications separately, so this combined rank does not have to carry the entire science story.
pages.note: Rank 1 is best. The 2026 country profile is used for the latest ranks and its uncertainty interval; no cross-edition score-growth percentage is calculated.

pages.label: 10 / LOGISTICS AND BUSINESS RULES
pages.title: Goods and business rules.
pages.deck: One index continues. Another was stopped.
blocks: The World Bank's LPI asks logistics professionals about customs, infrastructure, international shipments, service quality, tracking and timeliness. India's latest score is higher than in 2012. In 2014, the same displayed score had a worse rank, showing why the place in the list and the measured result are different.

LPI includes expert perceptions and survey uncertainty. It is not the number of ports, kilometres of road or delivery cost for every trader. The 2023 edition is the latest verified here, so it should not be labelled a new 2026 measurement.

Doing Business measured selected regulations through standardised business cases, mainly in Delhi and Mumbai for India. The rank improvement was large, but the index did not measure every business's experience, all states, corruption as a whole or the quality of employment.

The frequently quoted old rank of 142 comes from the 2015 edition, released in 2014. It is not the same starting observation as the 2014 edition above. A publication year and its title year can differ.

The World Bank discontinued Doing Business in September 2021 after concerns about data irregularities in reports. There is no current Doing Business rank of 63 in 2026. The newer Business Ready project uses a different framework and should not be joined to this old series as if the measure never changed.
pages.note: Doing Business 2020 is a historical result, not a present-day ranking. Its discontinuation does not by itself prove that the India figures were manipulated.

pages.label: 11 / PERCEIVED CORRUPTION
pages.title: Public-sector corruption.
pages.deck: Transparency International measures perceptions, with a defined scope.
blocks: CPI combines assessments from experts and business sources about perceived public-sector corruption. Here, 0 means highly corrupt and 100 means very clean. A higher score is better. India's latest 39 is above its 2013 score of 36, but still low on this scale.

The score does not count individual bribes. It does not mean 39% of officials are honest, or that 61% of all Indians are corrupt. It is also not a complete measure of corruption in private companies, illicit money flows or every transaction a citizen encounters.

Transparency International's score framework is designed for comparisons from 2012 onward. The three-point rise from 2013 is therefore more informative than simply comparing ranks with different country counts. Even so, a small change should be read with the sources' uncertainty, rather than automatically called statistically meaningful.

The 2025 score is one point above 2024 and the rank is five places better. That is the recent published movement. It does not establish a long, uninterrupted improvement: there are intermediate years, and a national perception index can miss very different experiences across offices and regions.

More prosecutions can mean more corruption, more detection, stronger enforcement or a combination. Fewer complaints can mean less corruption or harder reporting. Those administrative counts answer different questions from this index and need their own interpretation.

Direct experience matters too: does a service arrive without an unofficial payment, can citizens scrutinise contracts, and do complaints lead to fair action? Those questions show how institutions work alongside the broad perception score.
pages.note: CPI 2025 is the latest verified edition at the cutoff. Rank 1 is best; score 100 is the cleanest end of the scale.

pages.label: 12 / PRESS FREEDOM
pages.title: Freedom to report the news.
pages.deck: RSF assesses whether journalists can work freely and safely.
blocks: Reporters Without Borders, or RSF, examines political, economic, legal and social conditions, along with safety. It uses expert questionnaires and records of abuses affecting journalists and media. The index asks whether journalists can gather and publish news independently, without serious obstacles or threats.

In the latest edition, India's score fell by one point and its rank moved down six places from 2025. These adjacent editions use the current framework. RSF's assessment places India low in the global list.

A major methodological overhaul took effect in 2022. The older score also ran in the opposite direction. An old and new raw score should therefore not be subtracted to calculate a precise decline since 2013. The historical rank is context; it is not a controlled experiment across an unchanged questionnaire.

The publisher is a press-freedom organisation, not an Indian official statistical office. Its definitions, expert selection, evidence and weighting deserve examination. Naming those choices is more useful than assuming any international rank is either unquestionable or worthless.

Having many newspapers, television channels or internet users does not by itself settle press freedom. The relevant questions include who can investigate powerful actors, whether ownership or advertising pressures shape coverage and whether reporters face violence, detention or intimidation.

This is an assessment of the wider operating environment. It does not declare every article false or every journalist unsafe. Read it alongside evidence about incidents, laws, ownership and access to information.
pages.note: Historical and current methods are distinguished. Current scores are on a 0-100 scale with higher better; no numerical 2013-to-2026 score change is asserted.

pages.label: 13 / RIGHTS AND THE RULE OF LAW
pages.title: Rights, power and justice.
pages.deck: Votes, checks on power and access to justice need their own evidence.
blocks: Freedom House's 2026 score splits into 31 of 40 for political rights and 31 of 60 for civil liberties. It mainly covers 2025 events, not the percentage of citizens allowed to vote.

The 2013 ratings used 1 as best and 7 as worst. They cannot be converted into a made-up old 100-point score. Freedom House also assesses Indian Kashmir separately, so its India country entry has a stated territorial scope. This is not a single undifferentiated score for every Indian territory.

The World Justice Project uses household and legal-expert surveys. Its eight areas cover limits on government power, corruption, open government, rights, security, enforcement, civil justice and criminal justice. One overall rank conceals India's variation across them.

WJP says India's overall score decreased 1.7% from the previous edition. A matched pre-2014 overall score has not been established here. None is invented. The latest verified edition is 2025; an expected 2026 release is not treated as already published.

Part 5 gives direct Indian records on courts, prisons, policing and elections. These international assessments add their own questions and methods. Voting turnout, rights and justice each need their own evidence.
pages.note: Freedom House does not give the simple ordinal global rank used by the other tables. WJP rank 1 is best. No fake old overall rule-of-law rank is supplied.

pages.label: 14 / ENVIRONMENT AND GLOBAL GOALS
pages.title: Environment and development.
pages.deck: Two indices ask different questions and cannot share a score.
blocks: Yale's EPI combines environmental health, ecosystems and climate results. In 2026, India's air-quality rank is 175 and its score is 7.89: serious weaknesses under the chosen indicators.

Methods changed since 2012, so the rank difference cannot measure a precise deterioration. Inside the 2026 model, the publisher reports a ten-year overall score gain of 7.47 points. Poor current performance and improvement from a low baseline can coexist.
Part 5 gives the direct evidence on air, rivers, forests, emissions and groundwater. Installed renewable capacity is equipment; an emissions indicator measures a different result.
SDSN, the Sustainable Development Solutions Network, tracks progress toward the 17 global goals. Its research index is not an official UN ranking or a percentage of people counted as developed.

Its 68.33 differs from NITI's 71 because methods, indicators and targets differ. The goals began in 2015, so there is no 2013 SDG rank. The 2026 report combines observations from different earlier years.
The underlying issue still needs its own evidence: breathable air, healthy children or reliable water. A stronger result in one area cannot erase a weaker result elsewhere by simple addition.
pages.note: EPI and SDSN are separate publishers and models. Their scores are not percentages of Indians enjoying a good environment or a developed life.

pages.label: 15 / ECONOMIC CHART: ROWS 1-8
pages.title: Read the pair with its missing label.
pages.deck: Original Matrix figures first; the source explanation follows.
blocks: 4.7% is an old 2004-05 framework reading. The revised 2011-12 series gives 6.4% for 2013-14. New 2026 estimates use another base; the displayed pair is not one unchanged series.
9.5% is an annual-average CPI reading. A matched FY2025-26 annual 2.1% is not independently established here. August 2026 is 4.82%, a monthly annual rate; it cannot replace a whole-year average.
Broadly supported for the Centre, including provisional 2025-26 actuals of 4.40%. It is the annual borrowing gap, not accumulated government debt.
22.1% is close to revised Budget amounts; provisional actuals are about 21.8%. The old 11.7% denominator is not independently matched.
Now confirmed: 2013-14 deficit US$32.4 billion; 2025-26 US$25.2 billion. RBI reports 0.6% for the later full year. A smaller deficit share, not a surplus.
Endpoint bank-asset-quality ratios are supported. Recognition, recoveries, write-offs and loan growth all matter. The fall is not entirely cash recovered.
The provisional 2025-26 ratio is 1.55%. The 2026-27 Budget target is 1.5%. Keep the rounding, financial year and estimate status visible.
56.1% is a central-debt revised estimate. The old 51.6% is not matched here under one definition and GDP vintage. Centre-only debt is not Centre-plus-state debt.

GDP is annual production; deficits are annual gaps; debt is a stock of obligations. These rows therefore cannot be added together. The current-account release resolves the open item in Part 1, pages 24-25.

pages.label: 16 / ECONOMIC CHART: ROWS 9-15
pages.title: The other seven economic rows.
pages.deck: A larger economy, healthier banks and world forecasts are different measures.
blocks: RBI's current historical table gives 23.9% for March 2014; June 2026 gives 20.8%. Keep the revision and dates. External debt includes more than government borrowing.
The reserve date and denominator are missing. Goods-only imports and goods-plus-services imports produce different cover. This exact pair is not certified here.
Bank of India's 2025-26 annual report cites 15.9% growth in non-food bank credit at March 2026. Matching the old 14%, coverage and merger adjustments remains open.
The subsidy categories and GDP vintage need matching. CGA reports Rs 4.54 lakh crore of major subsidies in 2025-26; this is narrower than all welfare support. Exact ratio pair remains open.
IMF's July 2026 update forecasts 3.0% global growth for calendar 2026. It is a forecast for the world, not an observed Indian FY2025-26 outcome.
This needs the year, country weights and contribution formula. It is not India's share of world GDP, and the exact pair has not been independently reproduced.
Define the country group, real versus nominal measure, year and forecast status. Some smaller countries grow faster; this is not rank 1 among every economy on Earth.

PPP means purchasing power parity: adjusting money values for differences in local prices. A contribution to global growth concerns how much an economy adds to a worldwide change. It differs from its share of worldwide output.

Together, pages 18-19 cover all 15 economic chart rows. Where a pair is supported, its meaning is explained. Where its source or definition is still missing, it is not promoted into a verified fact. Two endpoints alone do not divide credit among governments, states, private firms and world conditions.

pages.label: 17 / INFRASTRUCTURE CHART: ROWS 1-8

August 2026 stock: 1.74 crore connections. A connection is not proof of regular gas use. PNGRB separately reports connected and billed households.
MMT means million metric tonnes. GW measures generating capacity. A lakh is 1,00,000; a crore is 1,00,00,000. Units describe what grew, so they belong beside the numbers.

blocks: Baseline 16.72% is August 2019, not 2014. August 2026 reported coverage is 82.24%. A recorded connection differs from reliable, safe water every day.

Official rounded historical pair: 248 km in 2014 -> 1,155 km in March 2026. A longer operating network does not count annual passengers or affordability.

The later 23 counts Delhi plus 22 new projects. Of the new projects in September 2026: 6 fully functional, 12 with clinical services, 1 with MBBS only, and 3 at other stages.

June 2026 backgrounder supports the four-lane-and-above pair. Widening an existing road differs from building an entirely new route through new land.
MTPA means million tonnes of handling capacity per year. It is the potential amount; actual cargo measures the amount handled. A capacity figure should not be called output.

pages.label: 19 / INFRASTRUCTURE CHART: ROWS 17-23
pages.title: The final seven infrastructure rows.
pages.deck: Date changes explain some updates; definition changes explain others.
blocks: The July 2026 aviation snapshot reports 74 in 2014 -> 165 operational airports. A count can include revived facilities; it is not a count of wholly new airports built from scratch.
The August 2026 official comparison gives 387 -> 846. College count does not establish equal staffing, teaching quality or treatment access in every district.
CEA: 248.554 GW in March 2014 -> 554.544 GW in August 2026. Installed equipment differs from electricity generated or dependable household supply.
109 is near 2014-15 capacity of 109.85 MT, not pre-2014 capacity. The 2013-14 capacity was 102.26 MT; June 2026 reports above 220 MT. Annual 2025-26 output was 168.4 MT.
Annual output: 565.77 MT in 2013-14 -> 1,040.08 in 2025-26. The latest level remains below 2024-25's 1,047.52 MT; a long rise does not mean a rise every year.
15,340 km in 2014 -> 27,427 operational km at December 2025, reported in the March 2026 MIS. Authorised or planned pipelines are different counts.
About 2.91 lakh in 2014 -> above 5 lakh in January 2026, for lines of 220 kV and above. Circuit km is not the same as route km.

The infrastructure chart's percentage usually divides the added amount by the later total. If 250 becomes 1,000, the added 750 is 75% of the later stock. Ordinary growth uses the earlier base: 750 divided by 250 is 300%. Both calculations have a meaning, but they answer different questions.

Neither arithmetic operation proves that a government created that share of the total. Plans, construction, commissioning, private investment and earlier assets can have different timelines. Pages 20-22 cover all 23 supplied chart rows; the qualifications belong with the achievements.
pages.note: The steel comparison separates annual capacity from annual production. Chart percentages are not measurements of political responsibility.

pages.label: 20 / CRIME, RAILWAYS AND DEFENCE
pages.title: Read the missing qualifier.
pages.deck: The same reading problems recur across different subjects.
blocks: 9,966 registered cases; rate 9.5 per lakh ST population using the Census-based denominator.
NCRB does not publish a rate there in Table 7C.1. A missing rate is not a measured 0.2.
Their rates are not published. Do not replace a blank or suppressed rate with numerical zero.
The 2024 table records 1 and 4 cases respectively, but no published rate. Absence from a picture does not mean no recorded cases.

Part 5, pages 9-10, reproduces the case and rate data for all 36 places. National cases fell from 12,960 in 2023 to 9,966 in 2024: down 2,994. Manipur alone fell from 3,399 to 289, down 3,110. Other places together therefore rose by 116. That arithmetic does not establish what caused the changes.

Registered cases are reports recorded by police, not all incidents that occurred. Population, willingness to report and recording practices affect comparisons. A place's crime rate is not a finding about the character of its residents.

The other railway chart labels 1,051 to 1,670 million tonnes as 'freight capacity'. Those are annual freight-loading amounts, meaning goods actually carried. The distinction matters. Its zero for a named automatic train-protection system should also not be read as India having no railway safety systems before 2014.

The defence chart's export pair, Rs 686 to Rs 38,424 crore, is supported. Its production headline of Rs 1.71 lakh crore is below the later ministry figure of about Rs 1.78 lakh crore for 2025-26. The 2026-27 defence allocation is about Rs 7.85 lakh crore, a spending plan rather than completed production.

The remaining railway and defence rows need individual dated sources and consistent equipment definitions. They have not all been independently reproduced here. Fleet totals and estimated nuclear stockpiles remain unverified.

pages.label: 21 / CONSUMPTION POST
pages.title: A sale is not a unique household.
pages.deck: The figures below are the Matrix post's claims, not a certified sales dataset.
blocks: The earlier period has 14 financial years; the later one has 12. These are not equal-length eras. They also do not cover all sales since independence. The post combines data-provider names but does not supply the full annual input tables needed to reproduce every total.

Its percentages use later sales divided by the sum of both periods. For air conditioners, 88.9 divided by 124.7 is about 71.3%. That is the later share of claimed sales across the stated 26 years. It is not a 71.3% growth rate, or the percentage of Indian homes with an air conditioner.

One person can buy several phones; an appliance can be replaced; a business can buy a fleet. Sales do not identify unique households or show how purchases were distributed between richer and poorer buyers.

The arithmetic interpretation can be checked even while the underlying totals remain unverified. To establish them, we would need matching annual domestic-sales or shipment series, with provider definitions and coverage. I have preserved all ten claimed pairs without treating those missing inputs as solved.
pages.note: One million units equals ten lakh units. Product categories and sales versus shipments must be held consistent before the totals can be independently certified.

pages.label: 22 / GROWTH, INCOME AND THE WHOLE SERIES
pages.title: Growth and relative income.
pages.deck: A relative lead can grow while a country's own growth rate falls.
blocks: The growth chart's footnote says nominal US dollars. That includes domestic price changes and currency movements; it is not real GDP growth. Its compound annual rate spreads the change between two endpoints across the intervening years. The endpoint in 2026 also needs its forecast or observed status.

India's displayed rate falls from 10.9% to 6.1% while its relative position rises. That can happen if the other economies' rates fall more. The chart therefore does not show India growing faster in its own later period on this measure. Its group also includes the EU alongside some member countries; it is not a list of every country.

EMDE means emerging-market and developing economies. If India's income becomes a larger share of their average, it has improved relative to that denominator. A falling ratio can occur even when India's own income rises, if the comparison average rises faster.

The income chart needs a stated dollar or PPP measure, a definition of the group average and one IMF data vintage. The exact ratio series and G20 endpoint calculations were not independently reproduced here. The 2031 number is plainly a projection, not an achievement already delivered.

The six volumes show substantial gains in networks, production and several human outcomes. They also show gaps in work quality, nutrition, clean air, opportunity and justice. Every conclusion keeps its own measure, population and date.
I want the reader to leave with a usable habit: read the number, read its label, then ask what it changes in a person's life. That keeps achievements and problems visible together.
pages.note: The two final chart series remain claims pending reproducible raw data and definitions. This closes the planned six-part, 168-page series; it does not claim an exhaustive audit of every Matrix post.
